differentiator: "Trust layer for AI agents" — blockchain-based KYA / KYD identity and governance infrastructure for the agentic economy.

name: Hush Security
capabilities: Secretless, policy-based machine and non-human/agent access; discovery and inventory of machine identities; runtime visibility and control over machine-to-machine access.
sensors: Runtime enforcement issuing short-lived, policy-based credentials that expire after use; replaces vaults/secrets.
protections: Eliminates standing secrets/keys; dynamic identity-based access; blocks credential theft and leaked-secret risk.
differentiator: "No vaults" secretless access platform for the era of agentic AI; team behind Meta Networks (acquired by Proofpoint).

name: ActiveFence
capabilities: AI safety, security and trust: red teaming, content/threat detection (disinformation, hate, fraud, CSAM), GenAI guardrails, model risk evaluation.
sensors: API/SDK integration into GenAI apps and platforms; runtime moderation of model inputs/outputs.
protections: Real-time guardrails and content moderation for GenAI; abuse and harmful-content blocking.
differentiator: Established trust & safety leader (clients incl. NVIDIA, Amazon, TikTok, Cohere) pivoting to AI model security; rebranding as Alice.

name: GraphnAI
capabilities: Identity security: AD/Entra ID config analysis, over-permission and stale-account detection, graph-based attack-path analysis, blast-radius and remediation simulation; real-time threat detection (brute force, password spray, Kerberoasting, DCSync, Tier-0 changes).
sensors: Read integration to Active Directory / Entra ID; graph engine over identity inventory.
protections: Safe remediation with automatic rollback if a change breaks; attack-path closure.
differentiator: Patent-pending FidelID technology; finds, simulates, and safely remediates identity risk with auto-rollback.

name: Styrk
capabilities: LLM/GenAI guardrails; AI model vulnerability assessment, adversarial robustness testing, bias detection, and privacy protection for AI models.
sensors: Guardrail layer on LLM input/output; model scanning/testing pipeline.
protections: Measure, monitor, and mitigate AI model vulnerabilities; runtime LLM/GenAI guardrails.
differentiator: "Guardrails of AI" — combined model-vulnerability testing and runtime GenAI guardrails; available via Carahsoft for public sector.

name: Maro
capabilities: Cognitive security: real-time, browser-level behavioral interventions against social engineering, insider threats, and ungoverned AI usage; AI usage governance and policy enforcement.
sensors: Browser-level instrumentation observing user actions in real time.
protections: Real-time intervention to stop risky actions before incidents; AI-usage policy enforcement.
differentiator: "Cognitive security" focused on human risk + shadow-AI usage; founders previously built Komand and Threat Stack.

name: ChatSee
capabilities: Runtime assurance / "failure intelligence" for enterprise AI agents: unified telemetry, execution traces, semantic drift + policy-violation + behavioral-anomaly detection, behavioral taxonomy, failure-pattern discovery, compliance tagging, dynamic prompt adaptation and model-improvement loops.
sensors: Guardian Agent control layer across decisioning/interaction/workflow agents; 100+ integrations across foundation models, agent frameworks, SIEM/observability, cloud, and data platforms — no architectural changes.
protections: Detect behavioral drift and policy violations at runtime, real-time alerting, automated failure response; shared "failure memory" feeding corrective actions.
differentiator: Positions runtime security/governance as a "reliability layer"; distills non-deterministic anomalies into 167 canonical failure modes; founder Sekhar Sarukkai built Skyhigh Networks (McAfee), Securent (Cisco), Confluent (Oracle).

name: Jazz Security
capabilities: AI-native data loss prevention that replaces rule-based DLP with context-aware understanding of data, systems, people and business intent. Detection across apps/desktop/cloud/GenAI, risk mapping, behavioral insights, plain-language policies (no rule writing), contextual blocking, and an agentic investigator ("Melody") that returns pre-investigated answers instead of raw alerts.
sensors: One lightweight endpoint agent at user space, <1% CPU, no integrations needed. Captures all user actions — copy/paste, screenshots, GenAI prompts, screen shares, file uploads, shadow IT, and personal cloud syncs.
protections: Precision contextual blocking of risky data movement with minimal business friction; GenAI/shadow-AI usage visibility and control; privacy-preserving monitoring and retention.
differentiator: AI DLP claiming 99% false-positive reduction via deep context; agentic auto-investigation of every incident. Founders are Unit 81 veterans and alumni of Axonius and Laminar.

name: NewCore
capabilities: Security-first workforce identity platform for the agentic era — humans, machines, service accounts, contractors and AI agents. Continuously discovers and maps every identity across directory, systems, PAM and AI; phishing-resistant passwordless auth with device-bound sessions; lifecycle governance and least-privilege provisioning for agentic identities legacy IDPs can't handle.
sensors: Enterprise-wide identity discovery and mapping across directory/system/PAM/AI sources.
protections: Phishing-resistant device-bound authentication, breach prevention with no single point of compromise, least-privilege access brokering and lifecycle controls for human and AI-agent identities.
differentiator: Positioned head-to-head vs Microsoft and Okta for the agentic era; $300M valuation at stealth exit. CEO Zohar Alon previously founded Dome9 (acquired by Check Point); CTO Amihai Neiderman.

name: Keep Aware
capabilities: Enterprise browser security delivering visibility and detection & response for work and AI activity inside the browser: browser DLP, extension security and malicious-extension blocking, phishing prevention, and discovery/control of third-party AI and agent usage. Agentic browser intelligence turns telemetry into actionable insight.
sensors: Agentless lightweight browser extension across Chromium browsers (Chrome, Edge, Arc, Brave), Firefox and Safari; modern API architecture, silent deployment, no traffic proxying.
protections: Browser detection & response (BDR), real-time blocking of phishing/malicious extensions/data exfiltration, and unauthorized AI-usage enforcement at the endpoint browser layer.
differentiator: Human-centric, browser-native security that secures existing browsers rather than forcing an isolated enterprise browser. Austin, TX based; seed led by Live Oak Ventures.

name: Apono
capabilities: Just-in-time, just-enough privileged access for cloud; access governance across human, machine, and AI-agent identities; Zero Standing Privilege model; AI-driven access intelligence and policy administration; automated least-privilege enforcement (who/when/why/how-long).
sensors: Cloud-native access management platform; API/IdP integrations across cloud providers, data stores, and infrastructure; agentless policy enforcement layer.
protections: Automatic granting and revoking of time-bound access; least-privilege and zero-standing-privilege enforcement; policy guardrails on non-human and agent identities; audit trails on access requests.
differentiator: Acquired by 1Password (Jun 2026, ~$250M-$300M) to extend access governance across humans, machines, and AI agents; Zero Standing Privilege thesis for cloud privilege sprawl.

name: Mavs AI
capabilities: Contextual prompt security with synthetic data replacement (granular synthetic alternatives instead of masking); runtime threat detection (prompt injection, jailbreaks, policy violations); compliance enforcement and audit logging; LLM-agnostic (OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, LLaMA).
sensors: Cloud or private environment deployment; API integration into existing GenAI workflows; NVIDIA Inception Program partner. Sub-second latency.
protections: ~99% sensitive data secured before reaching LLMs while keeping ~95% of prompts running with full context; synthetic data substitution preserving context for model accuracy.
differentiator: Synthetic data replacement (not masking) to preserve context — addresses the 'security destroys context by masking' tradeoff.

name: Ent
capabilities: Intent-aware endpoint security: interprets user and AI-agent behavior before risky actions are finalized; assesses intent in real time (e.g. sensitive-file exfiltration during browser use) and intervenes pre-action rather than alerting after the fact.
sensors: Endpoint/workspace layer monitoring user and agent activity (browser, file operations).
protections: Real-time interception of risky actions based on inferred intent before data loss occurs; pre-action enforcement vs. post-hoc alerting.
differentiator: Founded by RiskIQ founders Elias Manousos & Brandon Dixon (post-Microsoft acquisition, Security Copilot team); emerged from stealth 2026 with $100M seed led by Decibel (incl. In-Q-Tel). 'Intent-aware' pre-action interception is the defining bet. SF based.

name: Mitiga
capabilities: Helios AIDR (AI Detection and Response) extends Mitiga's Cloud Detection and Response across cloud, SaaS, identity, and AI-connected environments. AI Insights validates alerts and recalibrates severity with context; AI Triage correlates activity across environments into structured verdicts; Mitiga MCP exposes investigation-grade context to external autonomous agents. Three pillars: defend with AI (noise reduction, faster triage), defend your AI (protect AI infra/agents/service identities as first-class assets), defend from AI (counter AI-scaled recon and credential abuse).
sensors: SaaS platform built on Mitiga Cloud Security Data Lake — full-fidelity, pre-processed, normalized, contextualized cloud/SaaS/identity telemetry; MCP server interface for agent access. No endpoint agent.
protections: Detection and response across cloud, SaaS, identity systems, and AI infrastructure/agents/service identities; defends against AI-scaled reconnaissance and credential-abuse attacks.
differentiator: Cloud Security Data Lake feeds AI with investigation-ready data instead of raw, low-context logs; extends established CDR heritage into AIDR; native MCP support exposing investigation context to autonomous agents.

name: LangProtect
capabilities: Three products. Guardia (employees): monitors unsanctioned AI tools, prevents data leaks, enforces policy, audit logs across 5,200+ AI tools. Armor (AI apps): blocks prompt injection/jailbreaks, scrubs PII/PHI/toxic content, secures RAG against data poisoning, controls agent tool calls at <50ms latency, LLM-agnostic (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Llama). Vector (agents/MCP): control plane enforcing policy across tool access, data retrieval, and system actions.
sensors: SaaS platform with inline guardrails for AI apps and agents; employee-side monitoring layer for shadow-AI usage; MCP/agent control plane. ISO 9001 and ISO 27001 certified.
protections: Prompt injection and jailbreaks; sensitive data/PII/PHI exposure; RAG data poisoning; shadow AI / unsanctioned tool usage; unauthorized model behavior and agent tool calls.
differentiator: Single platform spanning employee AI usage, AI application runtime, and agent/MCP control with sub-50ms inline enforcement; serves regulated sectors (healthcare, fintech, public sector).

name: Starseer
capabilities: AI-Verify (pre-deployment model validation via interpretability — detects backdoors, hidden capabilities, misaligned representations); AI-EDR (versioned behavioral detections running continuously across AI endpoints); AI-SIR (intelligent routing across model fleets by policy, cost, compliance with containment).
sensors: Mechanistic interpretability / activation analysis of model internals at inference; LLM gateway routing layer across model fleets.
protections: Block/contain on detection of backdoors, covert capabilities, misaligned behavior; policy/compliance-driven request routing.
differentiator: Inspects model internals via interpretability rather than only outputs — surfaces hidden threats invisible to output monitoring. Advisors Rob Joyce (ex-NSA), Gary McGraw (BIML); partners SCYTHE, OWASP GenAI, MITRE ATLAS.

name: Evo by Snyk
capabilities: Evo AI-SPM (inventory models, agents, MCP servers, datasets, plugins across repos; AI-BOM); Evo Continuous Offensive Security (autonomous, continuous adversarial testing, pentesting-grade); Evo Agent Scan (detects malicious tools, hidden capabilities, prompt-injection risks); Evo Agent Guard (enforces safety policies on agent actions, monitors tool calls, blocks risky actions).
sensors: Repo/CI-CD integration for discovery and scanning; runtime guard monitoring agent tool calls.
protections: Block risky agent actions; prompt-injection and malicious-tool defense; AI supply-chain security; policy enforcement across AI lifecycle.
differentiator: Snyk's AI-native security platform spanning AI-SPM, offensive testing, agent scanning, and runtime agent guard in one — extends Snyk's developer-security reach to agentic AI.

name: WideField
capabilities: Identity security platform spanning human, machine, and AI-agent identities — connects to IAM/SaaS/cloud via API to discover dormant accounts, overprivileged roles, and stale credentials; AI-powered authentication analysis of risky login flows and policy/MFA misconfigurations; post-authentication session monitoring and cross-user/cross-machine investigation for SOC teams.
sensors: API-based signal collection from IAM, SaaS, and cloud identity systems; session-level identity telemetry sessionized into verified evidence.
protections: Protects AI agents from external threats and the organization from agents via session-level guardrails and least-privilege access; manual, policy-based, or automated API-driven remediation; machine-speed detection of compromised or misaligned agents.
differentiator: Covers the full identity lifecycle at rest, in motion, and in use across human, machine, and AI-agent identities; turns identity telemetry into verified session evidence agentic-SOC workflows can reason over. Acquired by Cisco (feeds Splunk's Agentic SOC).

name: Cognni
capabilities: Autonomous data intelligence that maps, classifies, and labels unstructured data (emails, documents, chats) across Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace using contextual AI rather than RegEx rules. Shadow AI Guard governs what sensitive data flows into LLMs and copilots like Microsoft 365 Copilot; Insider Intelligence detects anomalous information flow for insider-threat investigation; Rapid Forensics reconstructs incident timelines and blast radius.
sensors: API-based discovery and classification across Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, and Microsoft Purview; human-like content understanding of unstructured data sensitivity.
protections: Prevents sensitive-data oversharing to GenAI tools and copilots by labeling/classifying data before agents can surface it; policy enforcement on AI data access; behavioral anomaly detection on information flow.
differentiator: Contextual, human-like content understanding instead of RegEx pattern matching — zero-touch classification with no manual rules, positioned as Copilot-ready data governance for the Microsoft estate.

name: AptaSentry
capabilities: Goal-based automated red teaming across text/audio/video/image (AptaRed), agentic workflow stress-testing for prompt injection/privilege escalation/data exfil (AgentRed), model risk evaluation with findings fed back into training (AptaResolve), pre-deployment model supply-chain validation (AptaBadging), real-time prompt/response monitoring (AptaSignal).
sensors: Inline runtime monitoring of prompts and responses (<2ms avg detection latency); adversarial mutation/seeding engine generating 1M+ attack prompts; live threat-intelligence feed.
protections: Block / flag adversarial prompts and jailbreaks at runtime; detect tool-call violations in agent workflows; block unvalidated/compromised models pre-deployment; continuous production evaluation.
differentiator: Closed-loop red team → retrain → monitor: red-team findings fed back into model training ("8x model improvement per cycle") rather than one-off reports; multimodal goal-based attacks plus MCP/agent tool-call inspection.

name: Repacket
capabilities: AI-native secure web gateway: shadow AI discovery, DLP on uploads/prompts, AI app governance, phishing/spear-phishing protection, content filtering.
sensors: Context-aware security proxy running locally on the endpoint (no cloud hairpin).
protections: Block/redact sensitive data leaks to AI tools, enforce per-app AI usage policy, block phishing/malware, session protection.
differentiator: Endpoint-local SWG purpose-built for AI usage visibility and control; YC-backed, ex-SpaceX/AWS founder.

name: Safety
capabilities: Real-time visibility and governance over every AI tool, package, MCP server, and IDE extension across the developer fleet; malicious/vulnerable package detection.
sensors: Developer-fleet agents/integrations discovering AI tools, packages, MCP servers, and IDE extensions in use.
protections: Block vulnerable/malicious packages; policy and governance over AI dev tooling; audit and inventory.
differentiator: Software supply-chain security DB roots (Safety CLI / PyUp lineage) extended into an AI development security platform spanning packages, MCP servers, and IDE extensions.

name: AccuKnox
capabilities: Zero-trust CNAPP built on kernel-level eBPF and the KubeArmor open-source project: inline runtime workload isolation/enforcement, CWPP, CSPM/KSPM posture, and AI-SPM tracking layered on the same control plane.
sensors: Kernel-level eBPF + LSM (KubeArmor) DaemonSet sensors on Kubernetes/VMs/bare-metal; cloud API connectors for posture.
protections: Inline workload isolation and least-permission enforcement of process/file/network behavior at the kernel; runtime threat blocking; posture findings.
differentiator: Architecture is strictly eBPF/KubeArmor kernel-level workload isolation — a hybrid CNAPP / Workload Isolation lane rather than an application-layer AI platform; AI-SPM is layered on the CNAPP base, not the core.

name: Secure Agentics
capabilities: Real-time runtime security monitoring and control for AI agents. Ships Adrian, an open-source runtime security engine installed in two lines that embeds in the agent to monitor its chain of thought with a reasoning engine, detect malicious behaviour/prompt injection/policy violations/out-of-remit reasoning before any action, and block or pause for human approval.
sensors: In-agent runtime instrumentation; reasoning engine inspects the agent chain-of-thought (not just I/O) while it plans.
protections: Detects prompt injection, policy violations and out-of-remit reasoning pre-action; pauses the agent for human approval or blocks the action.
differentiator: Polices the agent thought process itself rather than just evaluating inputs/outputs; open-source engine (Adrian) with two-line install.

name: A Security
capabilities: Autonomous offensive security and remediation platform: continuously discovers, chains, exploits, remediates and validates real exploitable attack paths the way an adversary would. Cuts through CVE/misconfig/posture noise to surface what is actually exploitable, with proof and a path to validated closure (Discover, Plan, Exploit, Remediate).
sensors: Offensive AI agents run attacks 24/7 across the environment under human-in-the-loop approval, scoped execution and full audit trails.
protections: Validates exploitability via real-world kill-chains (not theoretical findings), remediates broken paths, re-tests to confirm closure, and integrates into ITSM to auto-close the loop.
differentiator: Autonomous offensive AI built for the age of weaponized AI — proves what breaks and fixes it, not just another findings backlog; every move fully logged under human-in-the-loop control.

name: SecurityBreak
capabilities: AI threat intelligence platform focused on adversarial activity across the AI ecosystem: AI agent monitoring, prompt threat intelligence, and AI supply-chain scanning. Creator of NOVA, an open-source prompt pattern-matching engine to detect and hunt adversarial prompts in AI systems.
sensors: Monitoring of AI agents, LLM prompts/inputs, and AI supply-chain artifacts (models, packages); NOVA prompt pattern-matching rules.
protections: Detects and hunts adversarial prompts, prompt injection, and emerging attacks against models/agents; surfaces AI-targeted threats via threat-intel feeds before they become widespread.
differentiator: One of the first companies dedicated to AI threat intelligence — attacker-centric visibility into how threat actors target AI systems, agents, and models; founded by threat researcher Thomas Roccia (creator of NOVA, SANS Difference Makers Award).

name: GenseeAI
capabilities: Full-stack AI agent/workflow productionization platform. Its security product, Gensee Crate (open-source, github.com/GenseeAI/gensee-crate), delivers runtime safety for coding agents — Claude Code and Codex on native macOS — with real-time enforcement, system-event monitoring, and long-horizon provenance connecting agent intent to OS-level activity before risky commands, file access, credential use, or tool calls execute.
sensors: Native macOS system-event monitoring of coding-agent actions (shell commands, file access, credential use, tool/MCP calls), correlated against declared agent intent with long-horizon provenance tracking.
protections: Real-time enforcement blocking risky commands, unauthorized file access, credential exfiltration, and unsanctioned tool calls from coding agents before execution.
differentiator: Founded by Prof. Yiying Zhang (UCSD, cross-layer data-center systems) and Dr. Shengqi Zhu (ex-Google, large-scale ML/AI systems); pairs agent productionization expertise with intent-to-OS-activity runtime defense purpose-built for coding agents.

name: AuthMind
capabilities: Identity SecOps platform giving real-time identity security posture management and threat detection across human, non-human, and agentic AI identities. Patented access-neural-network technology analyzes every identity access flow and request across on-prem and SaaS/cloud apps; dedicated Agentic AI Identity Runtime Protection line detects and stops anomalous AI agent access as it happens.
sensors: Agentless discovery and continuous monitoring of identity access flows across cloud, SaaS, and on-prem applications; AI access activity graph correlating human, service-account, and agent behavior.
protections: Real-time detection and blocking of anomalous AI agent access, exposed/orphaned NHI credentials, and identity misconfigurations; posture scoring and remediation guidance across the full identity estate.
differentiator: One of the few vendors treating agentic AI identity as an extension of a broader NHI/identity-SecOps graph rather than a bolt-on module; led by repeat identity-security founders (Datablink/Watchguard, Cyren).

name: Silverfort
capabilities: Unified identity security platform (originally agentless MFA/ITDR for on-prem and cloud) extended with a dedicated AI Agent Security product line (launched June 2025) that governs what AI agents can access and protects their identities with the same controls applied to human users, plus an expanded Non-Human Identity (NHI) Security module. Acquired AI-native identity-security startup Fabrix (April 2026) to build a combined agent/NHI decisioning engine.
sensors: Agentless protocol-level visibility into authentication traffic across on-prem AD, cloud IdPs, and now AI-agent access requests.
protections: Real-time access policy enforcement and identity governance for AI agents and non-human identities, extending the same MFA/zero-trust controls used for human identities.
differentiator: Mature, late-stage identity-security unicorn (founded 2016, $222M raised) rather than an early-stage startup; included for its dedicated, newly launched AI Agent Security + NHI product lines and its acquisition of Fabrix to build out agentic-identity coverage.

name: 8Layers
capabilities: Identity Security Posture Management (ISPM) + Identity Threat Detection and Response (ITDR) + automated compliance (ENS, NIS2, ISO 27001) in one platform for European enterprises, via modules Octagon (ISPM), Thor (ITDR), and Compass (compliance). Inventories and risk-scores human, service-account, API-key, and AI-agent identities.
sensors: API integrations with identity providers (Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, Google Workspace, AWS IAM) inventorying identities, including AI agents, across cloud environments.
protections: Correlates signals across time and context to detect identity kill chains before they escalate; compliance mapping and automated posture remediation for European regulatory frameworks.
differentiator: Founded by three members of the founding team behind Devo (Spanish cybersecurity unicorn); Europe-first ISPM+ITDR positioning with built-in ENS/NIS2 compliance rather than a US-market-first product.

name: Oleria
capabilities: Adaptive, autonomous identity security and governance platform giving unified, usage-aware visibility across human, non-human, and AI/agentic identities. Continuously discovers access, flags oversharing and stale entitlements, and applies adaptive governance and remediation as agent fleets and copilots proliferate.
sensors: Integrations with Okta, Microsoft, Salesforce, AWS and other IdPs/clouds providing usage-aware identity and access telemetry.
protections: Adaptive, risk-based access governance and remediation across human, non-human, and AI-agent identities; reduces standing privilege and oversharing risk introduced by copilots and agents.
differentiator: Founded by former Salesforce Chief Trust Officer Jim Alkove and ex-JumpCloud CPO Jagadeesh Kunda; positions identity as the control point for enterprise AI adoption rather than a bolt-on AI module.

name: Redblock
capabilities: Agentic AI platform that extends identity governance to "disconnected" applications the existing IAM/IGA stack can't reach — the 80-90% of enterprise apps lacking native identity integration. Purpose-built agents execute identity actions (provisioning, deprovisioning, entitlement management) inside those apps under deterministic, auditable guardrails.
sensors: Direct automation into disconnected/long-tail business applications via agentic workflows, layered on top of existing SailPoint/Saviynt IGA deployments.
protections: Deterministic, scoped identity-action guardrails ("AI assists, it does not decide") with full auditability for provisioning/deprovisioning/entitlement changes in apps outside IAM/IGA coverage.
differentiator: Targets the last-mile identity gap — disconnected apps — rather than competing head-on with core IGA platforms; deterministic, non-autonomous-decision framing distinguishes it from more autonomous agent-security vendors.

name: Scalekit
capabilities: Auth stack purpose-built for AI agents: OAuth 2.1 authorization server for MCP servers, delegated/ephemeral agent identity, per-tenant encrypted token vaulting, and enterprise SSO/SCIM, so agents act as specific scoped users rather than over-privileged static service accounts.
sensors: Sits in the authorization path between AI agents and 100+ prebuilt connectors (Gmail, Salesforce, GitHub, etc.), issuing and vaulting scoped tokens per agent action.
protections: Scope-checked, auditable agent actions via delegated OAuth tokens; encrypted token vaulting removes static API keys/long-lived credentials from agent workflows.
differentiator: Developer-infrastructure framing ("auth stack for AI apps") vs. governance-first identity vendors — ships as drop-in OAuth/MCP auth infrastructure rather than a discovery/posture platform.

name: Offroad
capabilities: Agentic identity security platform where AI agents act as the identity security team — continuously discovering posture and runtime identity risk across human, machine, OAuth-app, and AI-agent identities, investigating whether access is still justified, and autonomously remediating or escalating to humans.
sensors: Continuous discovery across fragmented identity systems (IdPs, OAuth apps, service accounts, AI agents); at launch audited 2,890 public OAuth apps in the Google Workspace and GitHub marketplaces.
protections: Autonomous investigation and remediation of identity risk (vs. alert-only tooling); direct action where safe, human-in-the-loop escalation with full context otherwise.
differentiator: Moves from identity visibility to identity resolution — agents investigate and close findings rather than just generating alerts; founding CTO helped build Palo Alto Networks' Cortex platform.

name: AKA Identity
capabilities: AI-native identity management platform providing visibility, intelligence, and action ("VIA") across fragmented IAM/IGA data — ingesting identity and access data across systems, applying AI/analytics to surface hidden risk (orphaned accounts, over-permissioning), and enabling direct, RBAC-gated remediation to move organizations toward dynamic, context-aware access control.
sensors: Ingests identity and access data across IAM/IGA systems and business applications to build a unified analytics layer.
protections: Surfaces orphaned accounts, over-permissioning, and access risk with AI-driven analytics; RBAC-gated direct remediation actions.
differentiator: Founded by former Forgepoint Capital identity investor Will Lin — an investor-turned-operator lens on where legacy IGA tooling breaks down for modern, dynamic access needs.

name: Fabrix
capabilities: AI-native identity and access intelligence platform mapping human and non-human identities (bots, API keys, service accounts, AI agents) agentlessly into an identity fabric graph, then using purpose-trained AI agents to automate IAM workflows and enforce least privilege — closing non-human-identity blind spots legacy IGA misses.
sensors: Agentless connectors building an identity/permission fabric graph across human and non-human identities.
protections: Least-privilege enforcement and automated IAM workflows driven off the identity fabric graph; purpose-built to close NHI blind spots.
differentiator: Acquired by Silverfort (Apr 2026), ~7 months after emerging from stealth, to build a combined agent/NHI identity decisioning engine; founders came from Run:ai (acquired by NVIDIA) and Orca Security/Microsoft Entra.

name: aizome
capabilities: Control layer between employees building AI agents and the enterprise systems those agents access: automatic discovery of every AI agent (including unsanctioned shadow agents), risk scoring, identity issuance, and permission enforcement.
sensors: Integrations with Okta, Microsoft Entra, CrowdStrike, Salesforce, SAP; covers SaaS agents, desktop agents, on-prem systems and air-gapped environments.
protections: Validates agent actions before execution and enforces least-privilege permissions; tamper-evident audit trail structured for SIEM and regulator/auditor reporting.
differentiator: Full-fleet coverage spanning SaaS, desktop, on-prem and air-gapped agents rather than a single channel; ties identity, permission enforcement and audit trail into one control layer.

name: Oak
capabilities: AI-native Identity Operating System for the enterprise: an AI connector framework reaching any application across cloud, SaaS, on-prem and homegrown environments to build a live, continuously updated identity graph from raw evidence, covering human, machine, non-human and AI agent identities.
sensors: Connector framework ingesting raw evidence from cloud, SaaS, on-prem and homegrown systems to build a live identity graph of who/what holds which access and how it's actually used.
protections: Real-time risk decisions, lifecycle governance and root-cause remediation across the full universe of human, machine, non-human and AI agent identities.
differentiator: Unified identity graph spanning human, machine, non-human and AI agent identities from a single AI-native platform, rather than legacy IAM tools built only for static human users.

name: Pallas Security
capabilities: App-aware, object-level access control that sets policies per file, folder, or label.
sensors: Data-plane enforcement via skill-based connectors, native hooks that inspect and rewrite tool calls, and a proxy/MCP gateway.
protections: Object-level access control, intent-based detection (scoring actions against approved tasks), and an automated rule detection pipeline.
differentiator: Enforces policy at the object level (restricting access to specific file/folder IDs, spaces, or channels) rather than coarse tool or application-level permissions.

name: PrivacyScrubber
capabilities: Zero-Trust Data Sanitization (ZTDS) for enterprise generative AI workflows, letting orgs use public LLMs (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini) without sending sensitive data to any external server.
sensors: Local browser-based Named Entity Recognition (NER) and OCR run entirely in-tab; ephemeral in-memory session maps wiped on reload.
protections: Masks PII, credentials and other sensitive data in prompts, CVs, NDAs, clinical notes and logs before they reach a public LLM; supports GDPR, HIPAA, SOC 2 and ISO 27001 data masking controls.
differentiator: Zero-Server architecture — no backend, API logs or cloud storage; works fully offline, giving a mathematical (not just policy) guarantee of zero data exfiltration.

name: Senthex
capabilities: EU runtime layer sitting between AI agents and model providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Mistral, Azure OpenAI), hosted in Germany for data sovereignty.
sensors: Drop-in proxy via base_url swap, a langchain-senthex package, or self-hosted Docker; works with any agent framework.
protections: 26 parallel guardrails evaluated on every call; audit trails built for EU AI Act Article 12 and Article 15 compliance.
differentiator: EU-hosted, sovereign runtime layer purpose-built for EU AI Act audit requirements, rather than a US-hosted generic LLM gateway.

name: Neo
capabilities: Prevents agentic threats across every device, browser, identity, and traditional application in the enterprise, giving SecOps real-time visibility and control over all human and non-human activity.
sensors: Device and browser-level agents plus identity-layer telemetry covering human and non-human (AI agent) activity across enterprise applications.
protections: Real-time detection and enforcement against agentic threats spanning endpoints, browsers, identities, and legacy apps.
differentiator: Founded by ex-SentinelOne President/COO and VP of Research; positions itself as EDR-style control for the full agentic attack surface rather than a single channel (browser-only or model-only).

name: Bloom
capabilities: End-to-end AI-native endpoint security unifying visibility, analysis, prevention, and response in a single control plane, covering interactions between AI agents, unknown extensions, and on-device data.
sensors: Endpoint-native sensors monitoring AI agent activity, browser/desktop extensions, and on-device data flows.
protections: Detects and blocks risky endpoint-AI interactions, unauthorized extensions, and on-device data exposure; unified prevention and response workflow.
differentiator: Founding team out of Palo Alto Networks/Dig Security/Demisto/XM Cyber; treats the endpoint itself (not just the browser or the model) as the primary AI attack surface.

name: Push Security
capabilities: Secure enterprise browser extension for the AI era, combining high-fidelity browser telemetry, real-time control, and autonomous agents to stop identity attacks, secure AI usage, harden identities, and prevent data loss without migrating to a new browser.
sensors: Browser extension telemetry across every site and SaaS/AI app a user visits, capturing logins, session tokens, form fills, and AI tool usage in real time.
protections: Real-time detection and blocking of zero-day phishing, credential stuffing, and session hijacking; identity attack surface hardening (weak/reused passwords, unmanaged SSO, unsanctioned AI app logins); autonomous in-browser response.
differentiator: Founded by former MWR InfoSecurity red/blue team practitioners; secures identity and AI usage from inside users' existing browsers instead of requiring an enterprise browser swap.

name: Burgus
capabilities: Security and audit gateway sitting between AI applications and their existing LLM or MCP providers, inspecting model and tool traffic in real time and combining per-request policy checks with behavioral learning across agents, tools, and providers.
sensors: 4,000+ security checkpoints aligned with OWASP and MITRE ATLAS spanning LLM API traffic, MCP tool and data connections, and cross-agent collaboration; behavioral baselining of normal system activity to flag deviations.
protections: Policy-based security alerts, behavioral anomaly detection across multi-agent systems, audit trails and compliance-oriented reporting (NIS2, ISO 27001, ISO 42001), and bring-your-own-key support across multiple LLM/MCP providers.
differentiator: Builds a behavioral baseline across agents, tools, and providers instead of analyzing each model call in isolation, flagging unusual cross-agent activity and unexpected data flows; alert-only by design rather than inline blocking, giving security teams visibility without silently interrupting workflows.

name: KIPIO
capabilities: AI Operations & Security platform purpose-built for MSPs, giving them full visibility and real-time protection across all AI surfaces used by their clients, delivered as a repeatable managed service.
sensors: Discovery of AI applications and agents in use across client organizations, tracking which tools employees use and what data they share with them.
protections: Governance and compliance controls over AI tool usage against corporate policy and regulatory requirements, plus security controls against shadow AI, unauthorized access, data exfiltration, wasted licenses, and uncontrolled AI spend.
differentiator: Built specifically for MSPs/MSSPs rather than end enterprises, letting them resell AI operations and security as a scalable managed service across their client base.

name: Arrakis Security
capabilities: Autonomous Workforce Governance Platform delivering total visibility, policy enforcement, and real-time remediation over autonomous AI agents operating within enterprise infrastructure, spanning coding agents, assistant agents, and autonomous agents.
sensors: Automatic discovery of agents across SaaS, cloud, and endpoints with ownership tracking and behavioral baselines; pre-execution static analysis and CVE correlation to OWASP, NIST, and MITRE ATLAS; intent-aware anomaly detection and cross-agent contagion tracking treating the agent, its workflow, and the surrounding SaaS graph as the governance object.
protections: MCP gateway enforcement with allow-lists and DLP rules, granular kill-switches, and behavioral recommendations to remediate risky autonomous agent activity in real time.
differentiator: Staged governance model (Observability -> AISPM -> AIDR) maturing from discovery to enforcement to intent-aware response; dedicated Arrakis Labs research division publishing real-world agent attack research in "The Arrakis Chronicles."

name: Modus
capabilities: Context Warehouse: a system of understanding for enterprise AI that learns how a business actually works from the work already happening across data warehouses, BI tools, pipelines, code repos, docs and collaboration systems, keeps that understanding current, and serves every AI agent just the relevant context it is allowed to see.
sensors: Continuous learning from metadata and usage patterns across existing enterprise data/BI/collaboration systems, independent of any specific data warehouse, AI model or application platform; integrates with agents via MCP.
protections: Governance enforced before context reaches the model, so AI interactions receive only information the user or system is authorized to access; sensitive customer data stays within the customer environment rather than being centralized.
differentiator: Positions itself as infrastructure/context layer rather than a model or app, cutting token consumption up to 10x by composing only relevant, permission-scoped context per AI interaction instead of dumping raw access to enterprise data.

name: Collibra
capabilities: Enterprise AI control plane governing context and control across any data, any model, any agent; built on eighteen years of ontology/data-catalog engineering; data catalog, data lineage, data quality, and AI governance in one platform; governs 2B+ data assets for 700+ customers including 78 of the Fortune 500.
sensors: Automated data catalog and lineage discovery across enterprise data estates (warehouses, lakes, BI tools, pipelines) plus AI/agent inventories, mapping how data flows into and out of models and agents.
protections: Policy-driven governance controls scoping what data and context models/agents may access, data quality and lineage checks before data reaches AI systems, and audit trails supporting regulatory compliance across the data-to-AI pipeline.
differentiator: 5x Forrester Wave Leader and 2x Gartner Magic Quadrant Leader; incumbent data governance/catalog platform repositioning as the governance layer for enterprise AI and agents, giving it a scale and customer base (700+ enterprises) most AI-governance startups lack.

name: MineOS
capabilities: AI agents that execute privacy and risk management work across the enterprise ecosystem: system discovery, data classification, vendor intelligence and assessment autofill, DSR fulfillment and redaction, transfer tracking, and continuous risk detection. Ranked #1 Privacy Platform on G2; recognized by Gartner and Forrester.
sensors: Continuous automated discovery of systems, data stores, and vendors across the environment; classifies data and maps its flow and transfers for ongoing risk visibility.
protections: Agent-executed policy enforcement rather than documentation-only privacy programs: automated data subject request (DSR) fulfillment and redaction, vendor risk assessment autofill, and continuous monitoring that surfaces risk as it emerges instead of at audit time.
differentiator: Frames itself around "autonomous privacy" — AI agents execute the privacy workflow end-to-end (discovery through DSR fulfillment) rather than software that just tracks and documents compliance state for humans to act on.

name: ThreatBook
capabilities: AI combined with deep threat intelligence to defend enterprises across the security lifecycle: precise threat detection, automated triage and response, and risk reduction. Agentic portfolio spans two arms — AI for Security (agents acting on intelligence inside the enterprise stack) and Security for AI (defending the AI estate enterprises are building).
sensors: APAC-rooted threat intelligence network bridging Eastern and Western threat landscapes; free community tools including ThreatBook Investigator surface nation-state, cybercriminal, and emerging campaign activity.
protections: Automated triage and response agents that act on threat intelligence inside the enterprise stack, plus security controls for the AI systems enterprises deploy.
differentiator: Unique APAC vantage point for global threat visibility, operating the #1 security community in the region alongside a dual AI-for-security / security-for-AI agentic portfolio.

name: AIR
capabilities: Secures every layer of the agentic stack — skills, plugins, MCPs, and sub-agents, both external and internally built — so enterprises can adopt AI safely. Continuously discovers, vets, governs, and monitors AI add-ons before and after adoption.
sensors: Pre-installation static and behavioral analysis of AI add-ons to surface hidden risks, excessive permissions, and malicious behavior; continuous fleet discovery across sanctioned and shadow agents.
protections: AIR Control for fleet governance (configuration, identity, permissions policy); AIR Filter for pre-installation vetting of add-ons; AIR Defend for real-time monitoring and response to agent actions; AIR Safe Marketplace as a curated, pre-vetted source of add-ons.
differentiator: Treats skills, plugins, MCPs, and sub-agents as a software supply chain problem, covering the full add-on lifecycle from pre-deployment vetting through runtime enforcement rather than securing agents in isolation.

name: Avon AI
capabilities: Universal management layer for enterprise AI agent operations, giving business and technical teams control over how AI agents behave in production across any agent or model.
sensors: Continuous monitoring and analytics of live agent behavior, tracking accuracy, compliance, and drift from business goals over time.
protections: Continuous testing and knowledge governance tools that keep AI agents aligned and compliant, deployed today across regulated industries including banking, finance, and insurance.
differentiator: Deep integration across any AI agent or model as a universal management layer, purpose-built for highly regulated enterprises moving from AI experimentation to production.

name: Loopers
capabilities: Bare-metal, zero-delay circuit breaker for AI API billing that sits as a transparent reverse proxy between applications and LLM providers, enforcing spend limits before requests reach the model.
sensors: Reverse proxy intercepting outbound traffic across 500+ AI models, checking budget atomically in Redis before every request and watching MCP tool calls for runaway agent loops.
protections: Blocks over-budget requests with a 429 before they reach the provider, halts infinite agent loops, and governs MCP tool calls to stop catastrophic bill shocks and LLMjacking.
differentiator: Bare-metal proxy with atomic per-request budget checks and cryptographic proof of enforcement, open-sourced under MIT as auditable Agent Runtime Governance infrastructure rather than a dashboard-only cost tracker.

name: Aikido
capabilities: Aikido Machine is an on-premises, autonomous AI penetration-testing appliance: a physical 4U GPU server deployed inside a customer's own data center that runs continuous white-box pentests against critical applications, with full source-code, dependency, and runtime access.
sensors: White-box analysis pipeline that enumerates exposed endpoints, admin routes, and feature-flagged code, then maps roles, data flows, and trust boundaries across the target application, including legacy stacks like COBOL.
protections: Chains findings into multi-step exploits (IDORs, broken access control, logic flaws), then validates each with a reproduction trace and a ready-to-merge pull request fix, running unlimited continuous tests across every release.
differentiator: Fully air-gapped: source code, docs, and runtime never leave the building, with local GPU inference, no cloud or third-party model APIs, and offline updates via encrypted USB, for finance, healthcare, and government compliance needs. Single annual lease fee covers hardware, software, updates, support, SLA, and GPU replacement.

name: Blaxel
capabilities: Cloud infrastructure platform purpose-built for AI agents ("AWS for AI Agents"); sandboxed virtual machines that scale to zero after 1s of inactivity and resume in under 25ms with full memory state preserved; agent co-hosting infrastructure with APIs consumed directly by AI systems; compute accessible via API or MCP, auto-scaling with agent activity patterns; has processed billions of agent requests pre-launch.
sensors: Sandboxed VM layer sitting under agent workloads; MCP server integration for agent-native access; Y Combinator S25-backed cloud platform deployable via API without traditional cloud provisioning overhead.
protections: Per-agent sandbox isolation with sub-25ms resume eliminating cold-start windows that would otherwise force persistent (less isolated) processes; ephemeral scale-to-zero environments limiting blast radius when idle; state preserved across pause/resume rather than left exposed in a long-lived container.
differentiator: Founding team of six previously built ForePaaS, acquired by OVHcloud — rare repeat-founder pedigree in this category; raised $7.3M seed one month after YC S25 demo day led by First Round Capital; positions squarely as infrastructure/DevEx play (like Daytona) rather than a security control plane.

name: Runloop
capabilities: Enterprise-grade infrastructure platform for developing, evaluating, and deploying AI coding agents at scale; Devboxes — secure micro-VM sandboxes with dual-layer isolation (VM + container) on a custom bare-metal hypervisor; Blueprints and Snapshots for environment management; Agent, Object, and Secret stores; Git-based state management; Public Benchmarks product giving on-demand access to SWE-Bench Verified and other industry-standard coding-agent evaluation sets.
sensors: Custom bare-metal hypervisor running micro-VM devboxes; SSH/CLI/IDE connections and interactive shell access; Reflex product for observability; VPC deployment option for regulated environments.
protections: Dual-layer VM + container isolation boundary per devbox; SOC 2, HIPAA, and GDPR-ready infrastructure; snapshot/blueprint model limiting drift and exposure between agent runs; sub-2-second startup and 100ms command execution keeping ephemeral sandboxes short-lived.
differentiator: Founded by Jonathan Wall, co-founder of Google Wallet and of Index (acquired by Stripe) — payments/fintech infrastructure pedigree applied to agent sandboxing; team includes alumni of Vercel, Scale AI, Google, and Stripe; leans into the "production gap" narrative — closing the distance between prototype coding agents and production-ready deployment — and backs it with public, industry-standard benchmark tooling (SWE-Bench, R2E-Gym) rather than isolation tech alone.

name: Hirundo
capabilities: The first machine unlearning platform, removing unwanted data, behaviors, and vulnerabilities from trained AI models without full retraining.
sensors: Automated evaluations and red-team testing across LLMs and non-generative models (vision, radar, timeseries, speech-to-text, NLP) to surface hallucinations, biases, memorized PII, and jailbreak vulnerabilities.
protections: Surgically edits model parameters to unlearn poisoned, malicious, or confidential data, biases, and hallucinated behaviors, de-risking models already in production without degrading performance.
differentiator: Machine unlearning instead of retraining or filtering — claims up to 85% reduction in jailbreak vulnerabilities, 70% reduction in biases, and 100% removal of fine-tuned PII with no impact on other functionality.

name: Cyberhaven
capabilities: Data security platform extended to the agentic enterprise: unifies DLP, insider risk management, and DSPM to trace and protect data as it moves through AI tools, coding assistants, and autonomous agents.
sensors: Discovers shadow AI agents and applications across endpoints, browsers, CLIs, and IDEs; monitors OS-level agent activity including coding assistants and MCP servers, capturing tool calls, data access, and multi-turn conversation context; proprietary data lineage traces sensitive data origin and movement across workflows.
protections: Real-time block, warn, and redact enforcement at the data level; risk-based policies govern data flows based on context; runtime guardrails on prompts and responses; redirects users to sanctioned tools; AI Risk IQ scores exposure across data sensitivity, model integrity, compliance, access controls, and security infrastructure.
differentiator: Built for autonomous agents rather than retrofitted from legacy DLP, using proprietary data lineage to trace sensitive data at machine speed across agentic workflows — well-funded ($250M raised, $1B valuation) incumbent extending an established data security platform into AI/agent territory.

name: Attestable
capabilities: Zero-knowledge proof platform that cryptographically verifies AI system integrity, letting organizations confirm a model's outputs were correctly computed from a specified model and inputs without trusting hardware vendors, secure enclaves, or privileged operators.
sensors: Generates succinct zero-knowledge proofs alongside inference that attest to which model, weights, and inputs actually produced a given output, working across CPUs, GPUs, and accelerators without specialized trusted hardware.
protections: Mathematically binds AI outputs to a verifiable computation trail, making it computationally infeasible to tamper with inputs, swap models, or fake results undetected, while preserving confidentiality of proprietary model weights and architecture.
differentiator: Software-only, hardware-agnostic zero-knowledge cryptography instead of trusted-hardware attestation (TEEs/secure enclaves), giving mathematically absolute integrity guarantees that don't depend on trusting a vendor or operator; launched from stealth with a $20M seed at a $71M valuation.

name: Fencio
capabilities: Zero-trust firewall for AI agents: learns an agent's behavioral boundaries during pre-production evaluation (Shark), then enforces those constraints deterministically at runtime (Prism), outside the LLM itself.
sensors: Prism intercepts tool calls and state transitions at runtime via SDK, network proxy, or MCP server wrapping; Shark performs pre-production AI red teaming and attack surface assessment feeding the enforced constraints.
protections: Deterministic, rule-based interception of agent tool calls and state transitions (written in Rust) blocks out-of-policy actions before they execute, independent of the LLM's own judgment.
differentiator: Enforcement happens outside the LLM as a deterministic runtime layer rather than another model-based guardrail, with pre-production red teaming (Shark) directly generating the behavioral policy that runtime enforcement (Prism) applies.

name: Orchid Security
capabilities: LLM-powered identity security orchestration platform that discovers unmanaged applications, maps their identity workflows, and brings them under IAM, IGA, PAM, and audit control, including agentic AI and MCP-connected identities.
sensors: Continuous discovery across on-prem and cloud applications, agents, and MCP servers, mapping authentication/authorization flows and identity posture gaps (weak or missing SSO/MFA, orphaned accounts, excess privilege) app by app.
protections: Remediation workflows that onboard discovered apps and agent identities into existing IAM/IGA/PAM tooling (integrations with Microsoft, Saviynt, CyberArk, SentinelOne), enforcing consistent identity controls and audit trails across the fleet.
differentiator: Uses LLMs to read each application's own identity workflows and auto-generate the integration/remediation logic needed to bring it under governance, rather than relying on manual connectors or a fixed catalog of supported apps.

name: I-THAM
capabilities: Cybersecurity platform purpose-built for AI, defending models, agents, data, and AI-powered applications with continuous monitoring across the AI stack — from prompt to tensor.
sensors: Patented Deep Stream Detection and Tensor Detection continuously inspect AI environments to identify vulnerabilities and detect attacks, covering prompt injection, model abuse, data poisoning, unauthorized access, and AI supply-chain risk.
protections: Responds to malicious activity before it impacts operations; lets security teams enforce security policies, manage AI risk proactively, and maintain compliance across the AI stack.
differentiator: Patented Deep Stream Detection and Tensor Detection aim to understand attacker intent and stop it before it becomes impact, rather than only detecting what an attacker has already done.

name: Keel
capabilities: AI control plane that issues signed "AI Permits" — pre-execution decision records (allow/deny/throttle/review) — for consequential AI agent actions, LLM provider calls, and MCP tool calls, enforcing policy and budget limits before execution.
sensors: Sits in the request path via provider SDK wrappers, managed-execution proxy (/v1/execute), or transparent pass-through (/v1/proxy); for MCP it registers upstream MCP servers and mediates each tools/call dispatch through the same permit pipeline.
protections: Blocks denied or over-budget calls before they reach the model or an MCP tool, caps spend before tokens are consumed rather than after the bill arrives, and produces tamper-evident, independently verifiable evidence of what was authorized and what actually ran.
differentiator: "Decide before, prove after": the pre-execution permit decision is the durable record, rather than reconstructing intent from logs afterward. Explicitly positions as a layer on top of existing IAM/IdP (not a replacement) with per-call MCP tool authorization rather than a registry, and published CSA STAR Level 1 self-assessments. Single-founder, San Francisco; private beta / design-partner stage as of Aug 2026.

name: Skuld Platform
capabilities: Autonomous offensive security agent that runs an entire pentest end-to-end: recon, planning, exploitation, privilege escalation, and reporting, across AD, Web+API, external attack surface, Cloud (AWS/GCP/Azure), and internal Network domains.
sensors: Executes 170+ real offensive tools inside a customer-controlled Runner, chaining recon and exploitation cycles against a human-approved scope and plan.
protections: Three-layer verification requiring every finding to be backed by an executed command and masked evidence before it ships; mandatory human QA approval gate for critical-severity findings; complete, auditable log of every command, output, and decision; enforced scope boundaries and real-time budget visibility.
differentiator: Full pentest lifecycle (scope to signed PDF report) run by a single autonomous agent rather than a scanner or a human team, with anti-hallucination evidence requirements and SaaS/hybrid/air-gapped deployment options.

name: AI Aramid
capabilities: Enterprise AI security control plane sitting between applications and every LLM (cloud or self-hosted), controlling every request before it leaves the network: a traffic gateway, real-time threat blocking, automated red-teaming, and model/behavioral risk scoring in one platform.
sensors: Proxy-level interception of all LLM traffic via the Gateway (no SDK or re-architecture, one config change), paired with Intelligence's behavioral analytics and risk signals across the entire AI stack.
protections: Shield blocks prompt injection, jailbreaks, and PII leakage in real time before they reach the model; Evaluator runs automated, CI/CD-integrated red-teaming against the OWASP LLM Top 10 and MITRE ATLAS, surfacing and prescribing fixes for every vulnerability found.
differentiator: Built to run fully air-gapped with zero data egress, unlike most AI security/governance tools that assume a live connection to a cloud backend for monitoring and enforcement. Kubernetes-native, so it drops into existing containerized environments instead of bolting on a separate system, letting government, defense, and finance customers adopt AI governance without routing any traffic outside their own infrastructure.

name: Neon Cyber
capabilities: Browser-native workforce security platform that protects work happening inside the browser — SaaS apps, GenAI tools, and credentials — with real-time visibility and control, rather than enforcement bolted on at the network or endpoint layer.
sensors: In-browser session monitoring of every user action: shadow SaaS and unapproved AI tool usage, credential entry, file uploads, and data movement across sanctioned and unsanctioned apps.
protections: Real-time AI guardrails and behavioral coaching at the point of risk — blocking phishing, credential misuse, and generative-AI data exposure without requiring users to be security experts; automated intervention during risky SaaS and AI interactions.
differentiator: Founded by Cody Pierce, who previously co-founded EASM pioneer AlphaWave (acquired twice), now applying that attack-surface pedigree inside the browser session itself: security travels with the user and acts at the moment of action, treating GenAI shadow-usage as one workload among many browser-native risks it governs.

name: Netacea
capabilities: Behavior-based bot management platform (Intent Analytics™) that distinguishes humans, legitimate automation, malicious bots, and AI agents across websites, mobile apps, and APIs, protecting against account takeover, credential stuffing, scraping, and other OWASP automated threats.
sensors: Agentless, ML-driven traffic and intent analysis across web, app, and API traffic — no client-side SDK required — fingerprinting automation patterns to flag AI-agent-driven traffic alongside conventional bot activity.
protections: Mitigates account takeover, credential stuffing, content and price scraping, and ad fraud; integrates with existing WAF/CDN stacks and adds virtual waiting rooms and traffic queuing to protect availability under automated load.
differentiator: Pre-dates the current AI-agent wave (founded 2018) as an established bot-management vendor, now repositioning its Intent Analytics engine to classify AI agents alongside bots and humans — arriving with years of production traffic data that newer agent-focused entrants lack.

name: HeimWall
capabilities: Free on-device macOS app giving engineering leaders observability into what developers paste into AI coding assistants (Cursor, Claude Code, Copilot, ChatGPT Desktop): detects secrets, credentials, and PII before they reach a model, without reading or storing prompt content.
sensors: Uses the macOS Accessibility API to inspect text as it's typed into AI coding tools, running 47 hand-written detection rules entirely on-device (no network calls, no AI models) in under 50ms.
protections: Masks detected secrets and PII with hashed placeholders before they're sent, and writes tamper-evident, hash-chained audit logs showing managers categories and counts only, never the underlying sensitive text.
differentiator: No signup, no account, no cloud egress, and doesn't sit in the send path, so it installs on individual engineers' laptops without blocking or slowing AI-assisted workflows, unlike gateway-based DLP approaches.

name: Nyuway
capabilities: Agentic AI security platform that discovers, governs, and protects AI agents and MCP connections across the enterprise, combining an MCP security gateway with per-agent identity and AI red-teaming.
sensors: Discovers GenAI usage, AI agents, and MCP connections across browser, IDE, and homegrown-app surfaces, detecting 110+ types of sensitive data (PII, financial data, secrets, credentials) in real time.
protections: Gateway-enforced policy for MCP traffic and agent-to-agent calls, per-agent identity and access control, and adversarial AI red-teaming (ARTP) to surface prompt-injection and agentic exploits before deployment.
differentiator: Bootstrapped and lean (7 employees), covering the full agentic stack — employee, developer, and homegrown-app guards plus an MCP gateway, agent identity, red-teaming, and model scanning — under one platform rather than a single point product.

name: Torii
capabilities: SaaS management platform pivoted toward AI governance: "Eko", an AI governance copilot that continuously discovers every SaaS app, identity, and AI tool in use — including shadow IT — and governs access and spend on top of real-time data.
sensors: Continuous discovery of SaaS apps, identities, entitlements, and AI tool usage (including shadow AI), plus an AI dashboard tracking which users and models are consuming the most tokens.
protections: AI-driven risk detection that flags hidden risk patterns and waste with explainable reasoning behind each recommendation, automated governance workflows, and a real-time ledger of app/identity/entitlement changes for audit readiness.
differentiator: Originally a SaaS management platform (founded 2017, $65M raised through a Tiger Global-led Series B) repositioning around AI governance — applying its existing SaaS/identity discovery graph to shadow AI and agentic tool sprawl rather than building AI security from scratch.

name: Sun Security
capabilities: AI-native agent security platform ("Own Your Agents") giving enterprises visibility, governance, and runtime control over AI agents across the full lifecycle: discovery, risk assessment, posture management, runtime protection, and compliance.
sensors: Discovers agentic tools and agents across workstations, cloud, and SaaS; profiles each agent from its instructions, system prompt, tools, and data connections; inspects every tool call and resource-access attempt.
protections: Guards against agents running without governance, supply-chain risk from unvetted tools, behavioral deviation, prompt injection, cross-tenant data exfiltration, and unauthorized data access.
differentiator: Full agent-lifecycle coverage rather than a single point solution; featured in Gartner's Market Guide for Guardian Agents 2026; publishes open-source security research including an "OpenClaw Detector" for spotting autonomous-agent tooling on managed devices.

name: SilverXAi
capabilities: AI red-teaming and security-testing boutique for LLMs, RAG pipelines, and AI agents, offering AI security assessments, red teaming, AI governance and secure architecture, an AI-driven SOC, vulnerability assessment, and threat intelligence.
sensors: Architecture and application security reviews, live adversarial attack simulations against production AI systems, continuous vulnerability scanning, and threat-intelligence feed aggregation.
protections: Defends against prompt injection, jailbreaks, RAG poisoning, data exfiltration, agent/tool abuse, and privilege escalation; governance work maps to NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001, and OWASP frameworks.
differentiator: Hands-on, boutique consultancy model rather than a self-serve platform — clients work directly with the person running the tests, rather than a product-only vendor.

name: aggrete
capabilities: Open-source MCP proxy sitting as a governance layer between AI assistants/agents and backend data connectors (Slack, GitHub, Drive, Jira, Salesforce, Notion), enforcing a YAML-defined policy on every tool call.
sensors: Intercepts every tool call before it reaches the upstream system, accumulates per-user activity/state with TTL-based memory across calls and sessions, and inspects inbound/outbound content for secrets and PII.
protections: Blocks requests that would leak a secret, cross an information barrier, over-share sensitive data, complete a forbidden combination of actions, or write out after reading untrusted content; also targets prompt injection, rug-pull attacks, and tool poisoning, with tamper-evident audit logging.
differentiator: Deterministic, non-ML policy enforcement that reasons over accumulated per-user, cross-call/session context to catch multi-step violations that point-in-time scanners miss; fully open-source and self-hostable in front of existing connectors.

name: Act Security
capabilities: Action-centric cloud security platform that shrinks the access surface instead of cataloguing findings. Cross-analyzes identity, network, and AI access together to map cloud constructs into business-aligned boundaries (organization, environment, application, data), then enforces deterministic least-privilege limits on what humans, workloads, and AI agents can reach. Scopes each AI agent to only the data, services, and infrastructure its assigned task requires, so an agent cannot ride inherited human permissions laterally across the estate.
sensors: Continuous collection across cloud IAM, network reachability, and AI access paths; measures the gap between configured, allowed, and actually used access to expose reachability and dormant permissions; policy-change simulation against production state before rollout. Ships the open-source Amphi toolkit (IAM Collect, IAM Lens, IAM Expand, Truth, Simulate, Shrink, Convert).
protections: Removes excessive and dormant permissions at scale through guided hardening campaigns; eliminates attack paths before exploitation rather than alerting on them; enforces access boundaries around AI workloads and agents; simulates changes first to avoid breaking production.
differentiator: Founded 2025 by the Medigate team (acquired by Claroty for ~$400M), out of stealth July 2026 with $60M. Argues that ~97% of cloud access sits dormant yet reachable, and that AI agents inheriting those legacy human permission sets — running continuously at machine speed without human judgment — turns latent access sprawl into live risk. Sells remediation of the access surface itself, not another posture dashboard; acquired Cloud Copilot a month after launch.

name: AariaSec
capabilities: Behavioral security for AI agents already running in production: detects hijacked or drifted agents that still hold every credential they were granted, so no policy is violated and nothing else fires. Learns a per-agent baseline — tool usage, data destinations, timing, token patterns — and flags when an agent stops behaving like itself. Never stores prompt or response text.
sensors: Content-free telemetry only: SHA-256 fingerprints of prompts and responses captured at the boundary, plus tool names, latencies, call bursts, and egress destinations. Per-agent learned baselines rather than generic thresholds; fleet-level drift detection; a debate panel of independent models argues each alert before it surfaces.
protections: Blocks destructive tool calls (deletion, data wiping) by default, with optional automatic containment. Enterprise tier adds kernel-enforced sandboxing via macOS Seatbelt, Linux Landlock plus seccomp, and Windows AppContainer.
differentiator: Attacks the gap credential-based controls miss — a compromised agent keeps legitimate access, so identity and policy tooling stays silent. Because the telemetry holds no content, AariaSec can publish PRAMANA, an open agent-compromise detection benchmark, including the attack classes where it scores worst: nothing in it can leak. Pre-revenue with three signed SMB pilots; San Jose based.

name: Andromeda Security
capabilities: Unified identity security and governance platform for the agentic era, covering AI agents, humans, and non-human identities (service accounts, API keys, tokens) across cloud, SaaS, and on-prem. Brings Access Intelligence, Access Management, and Access Governance into one platform so enterprises can retire fragmented identity tooling: identity security posture management with a live inventory and access graph, just-in-time self-service access with AI-automated approvals, agentic AI discovery and runtime enforcement, NHI inventory and risk prioritization, user access reviews, and joiner/mover/leaver automation.
sensors: Continuous discovery across cloud, SaaS, and on-prem identity providers building a unified inventory and access graph; real-time drift detection against baseline entitlements; behavioral and risk context per identity used to drive approval and review decisions; runtime discovery of autonomous AI agents and their entitlements.
protections: Right-sizes entitlements and removes standing privilege via just-in-time access; AI-automated approvals and access-review recommendations scored on real-time risk and behavior; runtime enforcement on agent access; automated offboarding to close orphaned human and non-human accounts.
differentiator: Founded 2023 by the Avi Networks team (acquired by VMware), Los Altos plus Bangalore. Frames AI agents as "the Third Identity" alongside humans and NHIs and governs all three in one platform rather than bolting agent support onto a human-IGA or an NHI point tool. Behavioral context, not static roles, drives every access decision. Customers include BigID, Endor Labs, DeepWatch, New American Funding, and TigerData.

name: Tines
capabilities: Workflow orchestration platform for security and IT, now extended into an AI-native build environment. Tines Stories automate investigation, triage, and response with integrations, human-in-the-loop steps, and AI orchestration. Tines 3B (launched July 2026) lets any team build AI-driven workflows while IT and security keep visibility, governance, and control over what those workflows and their models can reach — a governed blast radius for citizen-built AI automation rather than a free-for-all of ungoverned internal agents.
sensors: Full audit trail and run history over every workflow execution and AI-assisted step; central inventory of who built what, which credentials and connected systems each story touches, and which AI features are invoked. Runs on customer-controlled tenancy with a private, no-training-on-customer-data posture for its AI features.
protections: Governance rails around AI-driven automation: scoped credentials per story, approval and human-in-the-loop gates before consequential actions, role-based control over who can build and publish, and tenant isolation. Keeps enterprise data out of model training while letting teams delegate work to AI inside defined boundaries.
differentiator: Co-headquartered Dublin and Boston, founded 2018 by two ex-Docusign security leads; $272M raised at a $1.125B valuation, running 1B+ automated actions weekly for customers including Mars, Snowflake, Reddit, Headspace, and Fin. Primarily a SOAR/workflow automation vendor (AI for security), included here for the Tines 3B governance layer, which puts visibility and control over employee-built AI workflows — the inverse direction from the rest of this list.

name: Bold
capabilities: Endpoint-native data protection for the AI era: purpose-built models run directly on the device to watch how employees, copilots, and AI agents interact with data, apps, and services, then block, redirect, or coach before sensitive data leaves the endpoint. Covers shadow AI and unsanctioned GenAI tools alongside conventional exfiltration paths — browser, SaaS, email, chat, USB, and local files — in one on-device control point.
sensors: On-device AI that classifies data by meaning and sensitivity and infers user intent from behavior, with no cloud round-trip and no API gaps: every channel, app, file, and workflow on the endpoint, including prompts and pastes into GenAI apps and the actions of locally running copilots and agents. Because the sensor sits on the device rather than behind a SaaS API, it sees AI tools that were never onboarded or approved.
protections: Real-time enforcement at the moment of the risky action rather than alerting after the fact — block, redirect, or coach the user in-line. Policy covers AI tool usage (sanctioned vs. shadow) and what data copilots and agents are allowed to read or move off the device, with decisions made locally so enforcement holds off-network.
differentiator: Edge AI instead of cloud detection: models execute on the endpoint, so decisions are immediate, private, and free of cloud inference cost, turning the endpoint from a passive telemetry pipe into an active security agent. Zero-configuration deployment with pre-trained models — no baseline period, no policy tuning. Early customers report up to 90% fewer alerts, 95% faster investigations, and ~85% reduction in AI-related incidents. Founded 2024 in Tel Aviv by Nati Hazut (previously founded Polyrize, acquired by Varonis, and SAM Seamless Network), Hadar Krasner (CPO), and Omri Mallis (CTO); $40M total — $12M seed and a $28M Series A announced March 2026 — from Bessemer, Red Dot, Picture Capital, Cerca, and Wiz founders Assaf Rappaport and Roy Reznik.

name: Lava
capabilities: Security and management platform for AI data centers and neoclouds — the layer beneath the model. Builds one live cross-vendor graph inventory spanning compute, GPU fabric, networking, storage, virtualization, identity, and firmware/BMC, then ranks exposure and drives automated risk reduction and threat response across owned, colocated, and rented GPU capacity.
sensors: Cross-vendor discovery across NVIDIA, Dell, HPE, Supermicro, Lenovo, Cisco, Arista, Intel, and AMD estates, reaching below the operating system into baseboard management controllers, firmware, and the out-of-band management plane that EDR, cloud posture, and network monitoring never observe. Continuous configuration and drift detection against hardening baselines, with multi-tenant visibility for shared GPU hosts.
protections: Hardening-baseline enforcement and drift remediation across the management plane: internet-exposed BMC/IPMI interfaces, factory-default and unrotated credentials, stale firmware, weak tenant isolation and segmentation, shared monitoring that crosses customer boundaries, and machines reprovisioned without a full reset between tenants. Exposure ranking prioritizes what an attacker can actually reach rather than raw vulnerability counts.
differentiator: Secures AI from the metal up rather than the model down. Its FORGE framework — “harden the metal beneath the model” — ranks the top ten data center and AI infrastructure risks, five of which sit below the OS and are invisible to conventional tooling. Its BMCRadar24 research found 36,872 internet-exposed server management interfaces, of which 24,650+ leak IPMI password hashes before login via a 20-year-old protocol flaw (CVE-2013-4786), including hosts operated by GPU providers and neoclouds where a compromised BMC means tenant breakout. Founded by Elay Gliksberg (ex-Director of Engineering at Palo Alto Networks, founding engineering leader at Bridgecrew) and Yakir Kadkoda (ex-Director of Research at Aqua, formerly Israeli Intelligence). Funding and investors undisclosed.

name: PlainID
capabilities: Policy-Based Access Control (PBAC) platform — Discover, Manage, and Authorize modules — repositioned as the runtime authorization layer for agentic AI. Externalizes authorization out of applications into a central policy engine, then enforces it on AI identities: what an agent may access, which actions it may take, and what it may expose. Dedicated AI capabilities cover agent authorization, RAG security (filtering retrieved context to the requester's entitlements), and MCP Control for governing Model Context Protocol server interactions.
sensors: Distributed Policy Decision Points ("Authorizers") called at request time by applications, API gateways, data platforms, and agent frameworks; Integration Hub connectors for API gateways, data warehouses, and LangChain-style orchestration; policy administration point centralizes authoring while enforcement stays at the edge; identity data pulled from existing IdPs, directories, and entitlement stores.
protections: Per-request allow/deny on every agent action and tool call rather than coarse OAuth scopes; delegated authorization so an agent inherits only what the human principal it acts for is entitled to; RAG-time filtering that strips documents and rows the requester cannot see before they reach the model context; MCP-layer scope enforcement on tool invocations; full decision audit trail for compliance.
differentiator: Eleven-year authorization incumbent, not an AI-native startup — founded 2014 on PBAC for applications and APIs and raised $100M (including a $75M Insight Partners Series C in 2021) before agentic AI existed as a category. The pivot is a repositioning of an already-deployed enterprise policy engine: the same PDP that fronts banking APIs now fronts agent tool calls and RAG retrieval, which means existing entitlement models and enterprise IdP integrations carry over rather than being rebuilt for agents.

name: WithWings
