capabilities: Agent exposure management across the SaaS estate: discovers every AI agent and copilot — including unregistered and shadow deployments — maps the authority each one actually holds through inherited and delegated OAuth grants, shrinks that access to justified scope, and produces audit-ready proof that exposure went down. Delivered as six purpose-built security agents: observability (discovery and inventory), control (permission evaluation against policy), detection (suspicious behavior), enforcement (approved actions), mitigation (exposure reduction during incidents), and notification (contextual alert routing).
sensors: API and OAuth integrations across SaaS applications, inherited from the Wing Security SSPM graph — enumerates connected AI agents, copilots, and app-to-app tokens, then resolves effective permissions through inherited and delegated grant chains. Multi-tenant by design for MDR/MSSP deployments.
protections: Least-privilege scope reduction for over-privileged agents, shadow AI agent discovery and containment, policy-based permission enforcement, incident-time authority revocation, and continuous evidence of exposure reduction over time for audit and risk teams.
differentiator: Bets on preventive authority reduction over runtime behavioral detection — "a well-behaved agent with unbounded authority is the incident," and "bounding authority only has to be right once per agent." Founded 2020 by IDF cyber veterans (Galit Lubetzky Sharon, retired Colonel and ex-head of IDF cyber operations, is CEO; Noam Shaar, retired Brigadier General and former IDF CISO, is President), the company rebranded from Wing Security to WithWings in August 2026, pivoting its SaaS-to-SaaS SSPM graph into an agent-native exposure platform that is itself run by agents.

name: Patronus Protect
capabilities: On-device AI firewall for endpoints: discovers shadow AI usage across browsers, desktop apps, IDEs, and local models; inspects every prompt, response, and agent tool call in real time; detects prompt injection and jailbreaks; masks or blocks PII, credentials, contracts, and other sensitive data before it leaves the device. Free Monitor edition for detection-only visibility, paid Protect edition adding policy enforcement. Ships an open-source scanner library (Patronus Ark / patronus-security, hybrid Rust/Python) and its own small detection models on Hugging Face — Wolf Defender for prompt injection, Husky tool-call classifiers, Lion Warden, Orca Sonar document classification.
sensors: Local system-tray agent on user devices, servers, and nodes operating at the application layer — captures AI traffic by behavior rather than by provider domain, so it sees ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Copilot, Mistral, Perplexity, Meta AI, and self-hosted Ollama models alike, including unsanctioned tools. No cloud analysis: all inference runs locally, works offline and in air-gapped networks.
protections: Inline blocking and redaction milliseconds before a request reaches the model; per-provider and per-capability access rules; restriction of agent tool executions; policy violation alerting and audit trail of AI usage per app and per user.
differentiator: Everything runs on-device with no prompt ever sent to a vendor cloud — a GDPR-by-architecture posture aimed at German and EU enterprises that cannot route AI traffic through a SaaS inspection proxy. Small German team (Casdo Labs GmbH, ~2-10 people) shipping its own edge-sized detection models and an open-source scanner core instead of reselling an LLM judge.

name: Britive
capabilities: Britive ARC (Agentic Runtime Control) applies a verify-assess-authorize-observe-revoke loop to every privileged AI agent action: agent discovery in cloud platforms that onboards each agent as a managed identity with a named human owner; standards-based agent authentication via SPIFFE SVID, OIDC federation and API tokens validated per request; per-tool-call evaluation of requesting identity, target identity, tool, arguments and context through the Britive MCP Gateway; just-in-time privilege created inside the target system's own access model for a single task; command- and SQL-statement-level control; mid-task revocation driven by live identity and security signals; cloud PAM heritage covering cloud, SaaS, databases, servers and on-prem.
sensors: SaaS control plane with cloud-native discovery of agents in AWS, Azure, GCP and SaaS platforms; MCP Gateway as inline broker for agent tool calls; no standing credentials issued to agents; session recording down to keystroke level; integrates with existing IdPs and the customer's own cloud IAM models rather than a parallel permission store.
protections: Zero standing privilege for agents, ephemeral just-in-time grants that expire on task completion or timeout, per-request authorization of MCP tool calls with argument inspection, mid-session revocation on risk signal, command and SQL statement blocking, human-owner accountability for every agent identity, full transaction proof capturing prompts, tool calls, arguments and session replay.
differentiator: Cloud PAM vendor that pushed its JIT ephemeral-access engine down to the individual agent action rather than the session: privilege is minted inside the target system's native access model for one task and destroyed after, so there is no Britive-side permission shadow. Keystroke-and-prompt session replay for agent transactions is unusual among agentic identity startups, and the named-human-owner requirement forces agent accountability into existing IGA review cycles.

name: Akeyless Security
capabilities: Three agent-facing products on top of the secrets platform: SecretlessAI brokers agent access through the Akeyless Gateway so agents never hold a secret; Agentic Runtime Authority evaluates each request against identity, semantic intent, permissions and policy and constrains the agent to the authority appropriate for the task; Agentic Identity Intelligence discovers and maps agents and surfaces risky paths between identities, credentials and sensitive systems, exporting findings to SIEM and GRC. Underneath: secrets management, certificate and key lifecycle, encryption-as-a-service and NHI governance at claimed 220B+ machine-interaction scale.
sensors: SaaS control plane with customer-deployed Akeyless Gateway intercepting agent requests before they reach targets; monitors SSH, database, Kubernetes and cloud API sessions; supports both secretless brokered access and managed direct credentials (passwords, API keys, certificates); integrates with mainstream AI agent frameworks and MCP.
protections: No secret ever lands in the agent (no storage, no privilege buildup), intent-based runtime authorization, unauthorized action blocking, sensitive output filtering and masking, real-time kill switch for session termination, Distributed Fragments Cryptography with hybrid post-quantum encryption so no single party holds a full key, tamper-proof audit trail linking prompt to intent to policy decision to executed action.
differentiator: One of the few agentic identity plays whose credential substrate is its own patented DFC key architecture rather than a vault wrapper, so the secretless claim goes down to key material never being assembled in one place. Semantic intent evaluation as a first-class policy input distinguishes it from peers that authorize on identity and scope alone, and the machine-interaction volume from the secrets business gives it a behavioral baseline greenfield agent-identity startups do not have.

name: ClearVector
capabilities: Identity-driven detection and response for production environments, treating AI agents as a first-class identity type alongside humans, NHIs and third parties. Discovers every identity in production and attributes activity to its origin, answering who did what and when in 30 seconds to 2 minutes; identity graph maps every identity and interaction; detection engine flags rogue or off-the-rails agent behavior in seconds; single-click isolation of a compromised identity or resource without taking production down; unified timelines stitching GitHub, CI/CD, cloud control planes and in-workload runtime behavior.
sensors: Private SaaS deployed entirely inside the customer environment; in-workload sensors for containers, Lambda and EC2 giving runtime container visibility and attribution; cloud control-plane ingestion for AWS, GCP and Azure; source-control and CI/CD telemetry; available via AWS Marketplace.
protections: Detection guardrails applied to every identity including AI agents, post-authentication behavioral detection rather than auth-event or posture checks, one-click identity and resource isolation for containment, runtime attribution of agent actions back to the human or pipeline that spawned them, full production activity timeline for incident response.
differentiator: Operates after authentication and inside the workload, which is where an agent that already holds valid credentials actually misbehaves — a gap both ITDR and AI-SPM tooling leave open. Private SaaS running wholly in the customer's account suits regulated production estates that will not ship runtime telemetry to a vendor cloud, and the attribution model was built for DART/CIRT investigation speed rather than as a posture dashboard.

name: Xage Security
capabilities: Unified Zero Trust for AI layered on the Xage Fabric. Agent Sentry gives runtime visibility and control over AI agents — prompts, tool usage, API calls, outputs and agent-to-agent traffic — and assigns each agent a unique identity with an onboarding, credentialing and decommissioning lifecycle. Resource Gateway governs how agents reach enterprise resources over MCP and APIs, brokering every interaction through identity-based zero-trust enforcement across SaaS, databases, cloud services and operational infrastructure. Multihop identity and privilege enforcement traces permissions across users, agents, LLMs, APIs and data sources.
sensors: Overlay architecture deployed without redesigning the underlying infrastructure; distributed Xage Fabric nodes spanning cloud, SaaS, data centers, on-prem, OT and edge, including physical infrastructure such as servers, GPUs and power systems; covers corporate, vendor and BYOAI environments; tamperproof distributed logging across the fabric.
protections: Network-level least-privilege for LLMs, agents, AI pipelines and data sources, zero standing privilege with just-in-time just-enough access, time-bound delegated permissions, identity integrity preserved across multi-agent workflows, credential rotation and session governance for MCP and agent-to-agent traffic, data-leak and rogue-agent prevention through user- and agent-specific control of session, data transfer and command execution.
differentiator: The only agentic access-control vendor whose enforcement reaches OT, edge and physical infrastructure, which matters as agents start touching industrial and energy systems where a bad tool call is a safety event rather than a data-loss event. Its decentralized fabric survives network partition and has no single control-plane chokepoint — a deployment model built for critical infrastructure that the SaaS-gateway agentic identity cohort cannot match.

name: Speakeasy
capabilities: "AI control plane" for enterprise agent fleets, centered on an MCP Gateway that fronts every agent-to-MCP-server call through one URL. Central catalog of approved agents, MCP servers, and skills; shadow-AI discovery; SSO-backed agent identity; runtime guardrails that block prompt injection, PII, and credential leakage; full audit trail. Three paths to a production MCP server — generate from an OpenAPI spec, import an existing TypeScript server, or deploy pre-built integrations (Stripe, GitHub, Slack) — plus AI Cost Control, which consolidates spend and token usage across Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex per employee, team, model, and session.
sensors: Gateway-side interception of every MCP session and tool call, with distributed tracing and per-tool latency, error-rate, and usage telemetry. Client-side gateway hooks intercept MCP traffic at the agent endpoint (Claude Web/Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf, ChatGPT, Copilot, internal agents) to surface shadow MCP servers connecting outside the gateway. A device-resident agent collects AI session telemetry normalized to OpenTelemetry Semantic Conventions, tying activity to work identities even when employees use personal accounts.
protections: OAuth 2.1 with DCR and PKCE normalizing heterogeneous server auth behind one SSO connection (Okta, Entra ID, Auth0, SAML/OIDC); RBAC scoped at server, toolset, and individual-tool granularity, so each team sees only its own catalog; per-agent identities replacing shared service accounts; runtime guardrails that block PII and prompt injection before a call reaches its target; unified audit trail for investigation and EU AI Act / ISO 42001 / NIST AI RMF evidence.
differentiator: Came to agent security from the API-tooling side rather than the security side: founded 2022 by Sagar Batchu (CEO) and Simon Yu (CPO), the company built OpenAPI-native SDK, CLI, and Terraform-provider generation — still sold as "SDKs & CLIs" — then repointed that spec-to-server pipeline at MCP, launching the MCP Gateway in March 2026. The result governs the agent↔tool boundary as an API problem: the same machinery that generates a server also enforces auth, scope, and guardrails on it, so governance rides on the deployment path instead of bolting on beside it.

name: OneTrust
capabilities: "Continuous Governance" platform extending a privacy/consent incumbent into AI: continuous discovery and inventory of AI systems, agents, models, datasets, vendors, projects, and use cases, with ownership and lifecycle tracking; shadow-AI discovery for deployments that never went through review; automated risk tiering by use case, component, deployment context, or data sensitivity; built-in EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, and ISO 42001 assessment frameworks; AI Guard SDK for real-time inspection of prompts and responses.
sensors: Native connectors into Amazon Bedrock, Microsoft Azure AI Foundry, Google Vertex, and Databricks for model and agent behavior monitoring, plus the data-discovery and classification estate inherited from its privacy platform (data mapping, consent, DSAR tooling) to trace which regulated data feeds which AI system. AI Guard SDK instruments the application path itself, seeing prompts and responses before the model does.
protections: Policy-driven enforcement at inference — block, allow, redact, escalate, or route by policy — with PII and policy-violation detection in prompts and responses; approval gates and required controls per risk tier before an AI system reaches production; audit-ready evidence covering assessments, approvals, attestations, and enforcement actions.
differentiator: Governance distribution rather than security pedigree: founded 2016 by Kabir Barday in Atlanta as a GDPR consent and privacy-management platform, OneTrust reached ~$1.13B raised and a $4.5B valuation on privacy before repointing the same assessment, data-mapping, and policy machinery at AI. The AI risk register lands inside the tool where the privacy and third-party-risk programs already live, and AI Guard bolts runtime PII enforcement onto that governance record — the reverse of AI-native runtime vendors that start at the proxy and grow governance upward.

name: LogicGate
capabilities: AI Governance solution on Risk Cloud, its no-code GRC platform: centralized catalog of approved AI use cases and models with defined review and approval workflow; AI Governance Intake and Assessment Agents that autonomously triage submissions, route them to the right assessment path, evaluate them against risk frameworks, and create linked mitigations; risk identification across data privacy, algorithmic bias, and cybersecurity exposure, with continuous monitoring and quantitative risk modeling; framework mapping for EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, and ISO 42001.
sensors: Questionnaire- and workflow-driven intake rather than telemetry — AI use cases enter through submission forms and integrations with existing GRC records (third-party risk, enterprise risk, cyber risk), with shadow AI surfacing when undocumented use cases hit the intake queue. No inline traffic inspection or agent runtime instrumentation.
protections: Approval gates that stop unreviewed AI use cases from progressing, control and mitigation tracking tied to each model or agent, quantified risk scoring to prioritize exposure, and audit evidence across the AI lifecycle. Enforcement is procedural and human-in-the-loop, not inline at inference.
differentiator: GRC-native path into AI governance: founded 2015 in Chicago by Matt Kunkel, Jon Siegler, and Dan Campbell, LogicGate is a Forrester Wave GRC Leader (Q2 2026) that treats AI as one more risk domain in an application-builder platform, so AI oversight inherits the same no-code workflow engine, control library, and reporting as third-party and enterprise risk. Its own "GRC Agents" automate first-pass AI reviews — AI automating the governance of AI — but the product governs the paperwork around AI systems, not the traffic flowing through them.

name: Rogue Security
capabilities: AI agent runtime security across four pillars: AI-SPM (shadow AI discovery, agent inventory/classification), AIDR (detection & response), AI AppSec (build-time/CI-CD testing with the Rogue OSS red-team engine), and Access Control (approval + enforcement). RISC intent-classification engine flags malicious agent actions in milliseconds; Sentinel V2 model published as OSS on HuggingFace.
sensors: In-VPC deployment with zero data egress; endpoint + SaaS shadow-AI discovery, agent/MCP inventory, behavioral anomaly detection on agent workflows, CI/CD integration.
protections: Runtime guardrails at sub-5ms latency, prompt injection and jailbreak blocking, tool-abuse and privilege-escalation blocking, granular per-tool MCP permissions instead of all-or-nothing, remote removal of unapproved skills/MCP entries, automated containment.
differentiator: Focused first on coding agents (agents that ship code and hold production permissions); intent classification runs entirely inside the customer VPC. Rebranded from Qualifire (LLM evaluation and guardrails); the open-source Rogue agent-evaluation engine built there became the red-team layer of the security product.

name: MIND
capabilities: AI-native data loss prevention: continuous discovery and multi-layer AI classification of sensitive data across SaaS, GenAI tools, agentic AI, endpoints, on-prem file shares and email; context-aware detection of risky data activity; autonomous remediation via 'AI DLP Agents' that investigate incidents and tune policy; blocks unauthorized AI agent access to sensitive data. Covers data at rest, in motion and in use in one product.
sensors: SaaS platform connecting to data sources in minutes; agentless connectors plus optional endpoint agent; email and file-share coverage; real-time analysis of billions of data events.
protections: Real-time blocking of sensitive data leaving via GenAI prompts, SaaS, email or endpoints; user-guided remediation that teaches policy in the flow of work; autonomous incident handling; policy-driven controls over agent access to data.
differentiator: Rebuilds DLP for the AI era instead of bolting AI onto legacy engines — no regex or hand-tuned policies, live in minutes. Founding team of repeat security operators (Eran Barak sold Hexadite to Microsoft; CTO first employee at Torq; VP R&D first employee at Dazz). First data security company in Anthropic's Cyber Verification Program and first to earn ISO/IEC 42001; RSAC Innovation Sandbox finalist. $72M Series B (Sept 2026) led by Crosspoint.

name: AIBound
capabilities: AI security control plane that discovers sanctioned and unsanctioned AI, inventories models, agents, identities and data flows, and continuously tests them for misconfigurations, excessive privilege and sensitive-data exposure.
sensors: Read-only, least-privilege collectors across cloud and SaaS estates that map shadow AI usage, agent identities and the sensitive systems each agent can reach.
protections: A-F risk scoring on every AI asset, with high-risk deployments blocked before they expose data or breach regulatory controls.
differentiator: Built around a CISO-centric control plane that unifies discovery, testing and enforcement over models, agents and their identities instead of covering one slice of the AI stack.

name: Aigentsphere
capabilities: Enterprise AI agent management and governance platform that registers and onboards every agent, tracks performance and cost, enforces policy and generates compliance reporting against agent sprawl.
sensors: Real-time monitoring of agent behaviour, outputs and spend, with LLM-as-judge evaluators scoring output quality and risk indicators against configured tolerances.
protections: Policy enforcement from pre-built templates for GDPR, EU AI Act, ISO 42001, ISO 27001, NIST AI RMF and SOX, with critical anomalies escalated to human reviewers and remediation workflows.
differentiator: Runs the agent fleet like a workforce — HR and risk-management rigour applied to onboarding, performance review and accountability for every agent.

name: Bltz AI
capabilities: Agentic defensive security platform covering the full AI lifecycle: pre-deployment discovery and testing, runtime protection for GenAI apps and agents, and automated governance.
sensors: Autonomous defensive agents that continuously discover AI applications, agents and LLM-powered systems, then probe them for exploitable weaknesses.
protections: Network-layer runtime enforcement paired with automated remediation that patches discovered risks rather than only reporting them.
differentiator: Founded by former CrowdStrike leaders and built on self-healing defensive agents that close findings automatically instead of handing teams another detection queue.

name: CompFly AI
capabilities: Trust control plane for autonomous agents built on a Know Your Agent framework, giving every agent and task a versioned autonomy envelope enforced across models, tools, data, memory and delegation.
sensors: Live inventory across 50+ platforms that traces identity, intent, models, tools, data access and actions for sanctioned, third-party and shadow agents across sessions.
protections: Runtime policy decisions that permit, block or escalate before an action executes, with red-team simulation of agents and audit-ready evidence recorded in a TrustLedger.
differentiator: Autonomy envelopes are grounded in tested behaviour rather than static allowlists, so each agent's permitted blast radius is derived from how it actually behaves.

name: Dam Secure
capabilities: Security platform for AI-generated code that lets teams express requirements in plain English and enforces them across large codebases as coding agents write.
sensors: Continuous analysis of repositories, branches and pull requests, plus in-IDE and CLI inspection of code the moment an AI agent writes it.
protections: Blocks insecure patterns and logic flaws at pull-request time, with codebase context used to separate genuine vulnerabilities from false positives.
differentiator: Targets the logic flaws AI coding agents introduce — which pattern-matching SAST misses — and enforces the same standards no matter which coding agent produced the code.

name: Datawiza
capabilities: Agent Gateway that sits between AI agents and the systems they reach — enterprise APIs, MCP servers, SaaS apps, DevOps and observability platforms, databases and LLM providers — enforcing identity-aware access.
sensors: Inline inspection of every agent call, recording which agent or identity invoked which tool, which policy matched and what the outcome was.
protections: Validates identity tokens including Microsoft Entra Agent ID, evaluates allow/deny policy per agent, claim, MCP server, tool and action, protects credentials and routes sensitive calls through approvals.
differentiator: Brings a decade of identity-aware proxy engineering to the agent-to-tool boundary, so existing enterprise IdP policy extends to MCP servers without rewriting apps.

name: Lineation
capabilities: Zero-trust runtime security control plane for autonomous agents, combining observability, governance and active defense across OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Azure and AWS deployments.
sensors: A central control plane over LLM and MCP gateway traffic plus lightweight endpoint daemons that observe agent reasoning, decisions and actions at the point of execution, with auto-discovery of shadow AI.
protections: Policy-as-code evaluated at runtime, zero-trust non-human identity per agent, prompt-injection scrubbing, PII and secret redaction, approval gates and a kill switch on compromise.
differentiator: Enforces at execution through an endpoint daemon rather than only at the gateway, and keeps an immutable reasoning audit trail that can be replayed from prompt to action.

name: NuGuard
capabilities: Open-source-based AI trust platform for behavioural validation of agentic applications, discovering every model, tool and API in the AI stack and testing it before production.
sensors: Static analysis of agentic applications for structural risk plus sandboxed red-teaming of a running instance with 1,000+ adversarial scenarios covering prompt injection, MCP tool misuse, API attacks, supply-chain attacks and data exfiltration.
protections: A behavioural policy defined per application and validated continuously, with an AI-SBOM produced for the agentic stack and audit-ready evidence for deployment sign-off.
differentiator: Ships the red-teaming and AI-SBOM engine as open source with a hosted commercial tier, so teams can run behavioural validation in their own pipelines.

name: OpenBox AI
capabilities: Runtime governance and trust platform for AI agents that enforces identity, authorization and policy at the point of execution across long-running agentic workflows.
sensors: Native instrumentation of Temporal, LangChain, LangGraph, CrewAI, Mastra, n8n, AWS and Cursor workflows, with cognitive behaviour analysis that detects agent goal drift and dynamic risk scoring per agent.
protections: Actions verified before they take effect, human-in-the-loop controls on high-stakes decisions, cryptographic attestation and real-time audit trails, plus cross-organization trust for multi-agent deployments.
differentiator: Verification happens before execution with cryptographic attestation of each action, and the full governance feature set is available with no usage limits from day one.

name: Overmind
capabilities: Supervision layer for production AI agents that watches behaviour in real time, detects drift from expected behaviour and intervenes before damage occurs, targeting legal, healthcare and fintech deployments.
sensors: Continuous collection of production traces and agent interactions at the deployment layer, benchmarked to spot deviations the moment they occur.
protections: Intervention on harmful or drifting actions during live operation, with air-gapped deployment so proprietary operational data never leaves the customer pipeline.
differentiator: Founded by engineers who built AI systems for UK intelligence agencies, and feeds supervised production traces back into specialised models the customer owns.

name: Rein Security
capabilities: Agentic AI security platform bringing production context to application security, protecting custom enterprise agents that move money, touch confidential data and make customer-facing decisions.
sensors: A runtime sidecar inside production that records every database access, API call and agent action, building behavioural baselines from real code behaviour rather than static scans.
protections: Real-time blocking of deviations from baseline, plus posture coverage across code security, vulnerabilities, supply chain and compliance with ISO 42001, EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF and SOC 2.
differentiator: Inside-out AppSec: agentic data stays in the customer environment with no external gateway, and findings are validated against what actually runs in production.

name: TrustBound
capabilities: Control plane for secure, compliant enterprise AI that lets governments, universities, financial institutions and healthcare systems use AI without exposing sensitive data to model providers.
sensors: Interception of every AI interaction between users, agents and models, with immutable logging of each action for audit.
protections: Patent-pending tokenization keeps sensitive data inside the perimeter, with configurable guards that detect, protect and audit in real time, zero-trust verification of each agent action, dynamic access control and human oversight.
differentiator: Tokenizes sensitive fields before they reach the model provider, so regulated organizations can use external models without the data ever leaving their boundary.

name: VisIQ Labs
capabilities: Runtime trust layer for custom-built enterprise agents, controlling what each agent can retrieve, execute and approve across LangChain, OpenAI Agents SDK, LlamaIndex, Vercel AI SDK, Mastra, Semantic Kernel and Claude Code.
sensors: A trust layer inserted between agents and the systems they act on, discovering which AI is running and recording every action and the policy applied to it.
protections: Isolates agent data access, authorizes each action before execution with permit/deny/escalate decisions, routes sensitive decisions to human approval, and defends system instructions against extraction and override.
differentiator: Pre-action authorization for custom agents across many frameworks, with audit-ready receipts that prove what each agent was allowed to do.

name: Aptible
capabilities: AI control layer with an AI Gateway and MCP Gateway that lets teams use any model, connect any tool and deploy any agent under enforced access control.
sensors: Platform-level capture of LLM usage and agent tool calls, producing audit records without reconstructing them from scattered logs.
protections: Access controls and credential management on LLM and MCP tool calls, with audit logging over every agent action.
differentiator: Layers agent and MCP control onto an existing compliance-focused hosting platform, so regulated teams get AI governance in the same place their workloads already run.

name: AuthZed
capabilities: Authorization infrastructure for AI built on SpiceDB, the Google Zanzibar-inspired permissions database, scoping what agents and RAG pipelines may access.
sensors: Relationship-graph permission checks evaluated on every agent retrieval and tool call, with consistency guarantees and explicit delegation recorded per action.
protections: Post-filter authorization for LangChain and LangGraph RAG so retrieved documents are permission-checked before reaching the model, plus SpiceBox enforcement of fine-grained permissions on AI coding agents.
differentiator: The agent never decides its own permissions — SpiceDB does, using the same provably scoped relationship model already running in production at OpenAI and Workday.

name: QueryPie
capabilities: Access control platform extended to AI, exposing its policy engine as an MCP server so agents operate inside the same data and infrastructure access rules as human users.
sensors: Audit logging of every request and execution result across databases, servers and Kubernetes, including queries issued by AI agents through natural-language chat.
protections: Authorization enforced per identity so an agent cannot read data its principal cannot, with approval workflows retained for privileged operations and full traceability.
differentiator: Agent guardrails inherit an established enterprise access-control platform, so AI access policy is the existing data access policy rather than a parallel system.

name: Praegis
capabilities: AI-native endpoint platform combining shadow AI governance with ransomware prevention and zero-trust defense for enterprise endpoints.
sensors: Kernel-level behavioural monitoring derived from NSA research, watching process behaviour and unsanctioned AI tool usage on the endpoint.
protections: Blocks unsanctioned AI tools, enforces guardrails on approved models, applies universal encryption to sensitive data, and intercepts malicious processes pre-execution.
differentiator: Treats shadow AI as an endpoint problem, enforcing AI policy in the same kernel-level agent that stops ransomware before encryption starts.

name: Groovy Security
capabilities: Early-stage platform positioned around securing enterprise AI systems and automating security operations around them.
sensors: Public product detail is limited; the company describes monitoring of AI usage across the enterprise as the basis for its controls.
protections: Policy enforcement over AI usage paired with automation of the security workflows that surround AI adoption.
differentiator: Salt Lake City based and founder-led, pairing AI-system protection with security automation in one early-stage product.

name: Nudge Security
capabilities: Workforce AI and SaaS governance platform that discovers the full SaaS and AI footprint — apps, OAuth integrations, human and non-human identities, and user activity — within hours of deployment, with no agents or endpoint software, then scores risk and drives remediation through automated workflows.
sensors: Patented discovery method that reads the organization's email/identity provider metadata to surface every SaaS and GenAI account ever created, plus OAuth grant and API-integration inventory, AI app supply-chain and vendor security-profile data, and ongoing account/identity activity signals.
protections: Automated security guardrails delivered in-context through the browser and collaboration tools (Slack, email) to coach users off risky AI apps, OAuth-grant revocation and app blocking, MFA/SSO hygiene enforcement, offboarding and access-review workflows, and AI-usage policy attestation.
differentiator: Founded by the AlienVault leadership team (Russell Spitler, ex-CPO; Jaime Blasco, ex-CTO); discovers shadow AI and SaaS from identity/email metadata rather than network traffic or endpoint agents, and enforces via user nudges instead of hard blocks — treating employee AI adoption as a governance problem rather than a perimeter one.

name: Rivaro
capabilities: Vendor-neutral real-time governance control plane for AI activity across browsers, APIs, agents, and workflows: discovery of AI usage including shadow and ephemeral AI across models and third-party tools, identity-aware policy enforcement at runtime, and a traceable record of what AI accessed, sent, changed, or attempted for investigation and audit.
sensors: Interception of AI activity at the browser session, API, and agent-workflow layers; detection of sensitive data, prompt attacks, policy violations, and abnormal AI behavior in the intercepted flow.
protections: Real-time policy actions applied before a risky AI action executes — block, redact, alert, or require human review — plus evidence generation mapped to SOC 2, HIPAA, and GDPR controls.
differentiator: Provider-neutral control layer spanning browser, API, and agent workflows rather than a single AI platform, built around a four-step intercept → detect → enforce → prove loop that treats audit evidence as a first-class output. Early-stage (founded 2025, Portland, Oregon) by Jeremy Grant, ex-Senior Director of Product at 8x8, with a team drawn from Oracle, Jive Software, and 8x8.

name: Forever Security
capabilities: Early-stage company building "AI security for the ever-changing workspace": monitoring and control of AI agents on employee machines — coding agents such as Claude Code and Codex as well as assistants and agents inside the browser and its extension ecosystem. Public output so far is offensive research on agentic browsers (Gemini in Chrome, Microsoft Edge Copilot Mode, Opera Neon, Perplexity Comet, Claude in Chrome), plus field reports from customer deployments, e.g. stopping a coding agent mid-session after a planted AGENTS.md in the Downloads folder steered it to install a malicious npm package.
sensors: Watches agent behavior rather than the user: what an agent reads, what it rewrites and what it reaches for on the endpoint (instruction files, package installs, credential access), plus deep inspection of browser and extension internals — JavaScript runtime and prototype-level analysis of extension side panels, content scripts and the message channels connecting a page to a browser's built-in AI agent.
protections: Responsible disclosure and hardening guidance for agentic-browser attack classes its team named — BragJack (extension-driven hijack of built-in browser agents, CVE-2026-0628 in Chrome and CVE-2026-55945 in Edge, ~$20K in vendor bounties across five browsers), MaXSS (UXSS in the MaxAI extension, ~1M users) and Spyder (UXSG in the SiderAI extension, ~10M users) — threats the team argues classic EDR and browser-security tooling cannot see because they ride the agent's own privileges.
differentiator: Attacks the browser-agent layer rather than the model layer: instead of filtering prompts, it studies how extensions, side panels and built-in assistants share privileges inside Chromium, and has the CVEs and bug bounties from Google, Microsoft, Opera, Perplexity and Anthropic to show for it. Founded by researchers out of the browser/JavaScript security world (Gal Weizman, known for the WhatsApp Web CVE-2019-18426 disclosure and LavaMoat/MetaMask JS-hardening work).

name: Levo
capabilities: Unified API + AI security platform: runtime discovery of LLMs, agents, MCP servers and RAG pipelines, AI-SPM, AI red teaming, AI gateway/firewall, MCP discovery and security testing.
sensors: Passive eBPF kernel-level sensors in Kubernetes/cloud workloads capture API and LLM traffic without code changes; CI/CD integration for shift-left testing.
protections: Runtime AI threat detection and blocking of prompt injection, data leakage and agent privilege misuse; guardrails via AI gateway/firewall.
differentiator: Grew from API security: its eBPF sensors were already seeing LLM traffic, so it now covers API and AI posture from one runtime sensor.

name: Bluebear Security
capabilities: Security control plane for AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Codex and others): real-time visibility into agent sessions, tool use, code changes and resource access, with governance and audit trails.
sensors: Endpoint runtime safeguard on developer machines hooking into coding agent sessions; SaaS control plane on AWS.
protections: Evaluates each agent action against the task's intent across the session; dynamically scopes permissions per task, blocks out-of-mandate actions, protects credentials and secrets, and requires human-in-the-loop approval for high-impact actions.
differentiator: Targets the "mandate gap": judges coding agent actions by intent drift (unrequested refactors, banned dependencies, self-granted permissions), not static allow/deny rules. Founded by the PerimeterX founding team.

name: BeyondGuard
capabilities: Enterprise AI security control plane with dedicated guards across six layers: RAG/data ingestion, LLM inference and model supply chain, prompt orchestration, agent actions, MCP/tool integrations and response delivery; AI red teaming.
sensors: Inline model-agnostic proxy/control plane in front of LLM apps and agents; deployable on-prem or private cloud for data-residency needs.
protections: Blocks prompt injection and jailbreaks, protects system prompts, masks PII and financial data, filters toxic output, detects hallucinations and validates RAG answers; role-based tool access, agent behavior policies and plugin sandboxing; mapping to NIST AI RMF and MITRE ATLAS.
differentiator: Team comes from building AI inside banks, and the product is aimed at regulated financial institutions (e.g. Odeabank) that need security decisions kept independent of the models and deployed where their data stays.

name: Dawn Security
capabilities: Access Intelligence platform that connects identity and data in a live graph to decide whether each access by a human, machine or AI agent identity was intended and legitimate, not just permitted. Modules cover access discovery, access posture, access intelligence and access detection and response.
sensors: Agentless API integrations across the customer's SaaS, identity and AI stack. It rebuilds historical and real-time access activity within hours and needs no endpoint agents.
protections: Finds human, NHI, agentic and external identities, including unregistered agents and shadow AI tools. It maps the data each identity actually used, keeps classifying that data, and flags or acts on illegitimate access after authorization.
differentiator: It judges legitimacy by reasoning about the purpose of the access and the identity's history instead of using anomaly detection or rules it has to maintain. It combines the identity side (IVIP) and the data side (DSPM-style classification) in one platform, with AI agents treated as identities that have intent.

name: Rig Security
capabilities: Rig has an identity correlation engine (RICE) that links every account, token, non-human identity and AI agent to the human who owns it. On top of that it builds an access graph, does posture and attack-path analysis, enforces least privilege, and detects and responds to identity threats.
sensors: It connects without agents to identity, cloud and dev systems such as Okta, Microsoft Entra, AWS, Snowflake, GitHub and Kubernetes. On endpoints it runs Gatewatch, which sees AI coding agents and MCP servers including Claude, OpenAI Codex and GitHub Copilot.
protections: It removes excess privileges, finds privilege chains that lead to critical resources, and connects scattered identity signals into attack narratives. At the endpoint it blocks specific risky actions by AI agents running in a user's session, such as unauthorized data access, and lets approved operations through.
differentiator: Rig separates an AI agent's actions from the human whose identity and session the agent is using, so it can control agents without disrupting the employee. The founding CEO previously worked on the CTO team at Wiz.

name: Prizma
capabilities: A self-hosted AI gateway and firewall that inspects requests from employees, coding agents and AI apps to cloud and local models. It applies one set of policies for data masking, proprietary-code blocking, approved-model routing, budgets, and approval of agent and MCP tool actions. It also checks documents before they enter knowledge bases and agent memory, tests models against attacks, and keeps an inventory of AI components.
sensors: An inline proxy with OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible APIs that tools like Claude Code, Cursor, Cline, n8n and LangChain point to. It connects to MCP tools, corporate identity (SSO/SCIM) and SIEM, and is deployed inside the customer's own infrastructure.
protections: Masks or blocks personal data, secrets, documents, images and registered proprietary code before they reach a model. Lets requests through only to approved models within budget limits. Requires approval for agent tool actions, and an approval covers only that exact action and its parameters. Quarantines memory entries from untrusted sources to stop indirect prompt injection from persisting. Logs every decision to the SIEM.
differentiator: Matches requests against the company's registered proprietary code, so it can block algorithm leaks even when no secrets or personal data are present. Approvals are bound to one exact agent action, and a consequence graph maps an agent's permissions and tools to the resources it can reach. It supports Russian and Chinese models (YandexGPT, GigaChat, Qwen, Kimi, DeepSeek) and its site is in English, Russian and Chinese.

name: PromptHalo
capabilities: Model-agnostic platform that combines automated AI red-teaming (static probes, a prompt-injection library and PAIR adaptive attacks) with runtime enforcement over what AI agents are allowed to do. It also offers an agent registry with per-agent policies, multi-agent workflow topology and risk views, behavioral baselines, and audit trails of AI decisions.
sensors: Deployed as a security sidecar next to production AI applications, as an API gateway in front of LLM endpoints (OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama, vLLM, LiteLLM and generic HTTP+JSON), through agent-framework/orchestration integrations, and with a browser extension that captures chatbot targets for scanning.
protections: Inspects prompts and agent actions inline and blocks or flags prompt injection, retrieval poisoning, PII exfiltration and unauthorized tool or API calls before they execute. Each agent gets an identity key, passports and scoped tool permissions that can be revoked.
differentiator: Works without access to the model, its training data or architectural changes. It focuses on controlling AI-triggered actions before execution, and feeds red-team findings directly into runtime enforcement policies.

name: HOL Guard
capabilities: Open-source (Apache-2.0) local security layer for AI coding agents. It reviews shell commands, file access, package installs, MCP tool calls, plugins and skills before they run, and keeps a searchable local trail of every decision. An optional paid Guard Cloud adds synced org-wide policies, telemetry and team dashboards.
sensors: Runs on the developer's machine and attaches to agents through native pre-tool hooks, managed MCP proxies and launch integrations. Supports Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot CLI, Gemini CLI, Cline, OpenCode, Antigravity, Devin and others. Works offline with no cloud dependency.
protections: Applies allow, observe, ask or block decisions to destructive file and shell operations, credential and secret access, prompt-injection-driven commands, suspicious outbound transfers, malicious packages, unsafe MCP server configs, risky plugin or skill settings, and unsafe git pushes to production branches.
differentiator: One local policy across many coding agents, enforced on-device before the action executes. Built by HOL (Hashgraph Online), a DAO-structured standards body for AI agents on Hedera, rather than a venture-backed security vendor.

name: NopeID
capabilities: On-device security for AI agents running on employee endpoints. It discovers shadow AI agents, inspects each agent's reasoning, context, memory and planned commands before they execute, and enforces policy in real time. An enterprise tier adds custom scanners, central policy management, audit reporting and team access controls.
sensors: A local agent with a tray app on macOS, Linux and Windows. Analysis runs fully on the device, and telemetry leaves out raw commands, prompts, file paths, credentials and IP addresses.
protections: Flags anomalous agent behavior, skill injection, memory tampering, unsafe launches, intent mismatches and dangerous terminal commands. Responses include requiring human approval, suspending or killing the agent process, and quarantining the session. Untrusted agents can also be moved off the host into a remote execution environment.
differentiator: Pairs endpoint enforcement with a choice of where the agent runs, from native host controls to remote isolation, so risky agent activity can be kept off the user's machine. Pre-seed with undisclosed funding; co-founder and CTO Yaron Sumel was previously a backend engineer at Proofpoint.

name: Blast Security
capabilities: Preemptive cloud defense platform that turns security intent into preventive guardrails enforced through native cloud controls. Its AI agents use case maps what each human, non-human and agent identity can actually do, shows over-permissioned agents and service accounts as blast radius, and bounds agents by limiting which data sources, services and regions they can reach and for how long.
sensors: Agentless and proxyless. It connects to AWS, Azure, Google Cloud and Kubernetes and enforces through the provider control plane (AWS SCPs, RCPs and permission boundaries, Azure Policy, GCP Organization Policy). Nothing is installed on the agents and no traffic is routed through it.
protections: Denies unwanted cloud actions before they run, for any actor (human, AI agent or attacker). It replays months of real activity against each proposed guardrail to show which agent and pipeline actions it would block before enforcing, grants scoped, time-boxed exceptions when an agent is blocked, closes exposed surface such as public access by default, and applies guardrails to new accounts automatically.
differentiator: Agents are bounded at the cloud control-plane layer, outside the agent, so the boundary holds whatever permissions the agent inherits from identities, tools or pipelines. It does not inspect prompts or tool calls; AI agents are one use case of a broader cloud prevention platform. Founding team came from Solebit (acquired by Mimecast).

name: Aurite AI
capabilities: Kahuna, an agentic control layer that discovers, governs and recovers autonomous AI agents across the enterprise. It keeps a continuous inventory of agents, their tools and permissions (including shadow agents and shadow MCP servers), gives each agent a cryptographic identity bound to a human of record, and adds point-in-time recovery and rollback of agent actions.
sensors: Kahuna sits in-line between the agents and the systems they act on, similar to a gateway, with discovery across SaaS, browser, IDE, endpoint and any MCP-speaking agent. Deployable hybrid, on-prem or air-gapped. It enriches existing SIEM, IAM, EDR and DLP tools with agent-layer signals rather than replacing them, which lowers buyer resistance.
protections: Each agent action is checked as it is attempted, not at the prompt, so EchoLeak-class scope violations are blocked at the action. Irreversible or high-impact actions (moving money, shipping code, touching customers) wait for human approval, and a kill switch pauses one agent, a class of agents or all of them by identity, tool or data scope. Just-in-time credentials with delegation chains replace inherited standing privileges, and every action is signed for chain of custody, with audit logging aligned to EU AI Act Article 12, NIST AI RMF and ISO 42001.
differentiator: Discovery, runtime enforcement and agent identity are each offered elsewhere; what stands out is the combination. It treats legal-grade proof (signed, auditor- and court-ready records of what an agent did and why) as a core pillar rather than a logging feature, claims recovery and rollback of agent actions, puts all four building blocks in one control plane across SaaS, endpoint, IDE and MCP, and pitches itself as vendor-neutral and independent of model labs and endpoint vendors. The company started in 2023 building open-source agent tooling (the Aurite Agents MCP framework and Aurite Kai) before moving to agent security; Kahuna is offered to a limited design-partner cohort. Seed-funded by Corner Ventures, whose managing partner John Cadeddu is a co-founder.

name: Redecta
capabilities: Browser-based sensitive data protection for teams using public AI chat tools. Redecta detects and masks sensitive values in prompts before they reach ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Grok and DeepSeek, and can restore the original values locally in the AI response. A web platform adds team policies and masking visibility.
sensors: A Chrome extension (Redecta PrivacyMask) with a central admin panel. Masking and the mapping of original values stay in the browser; the platform receives account information and masking metadata, not prompt content.
protections: Pattern-based detection of emails, phone numbers, IBANs, card numbers, national IDs, addresses, passwords, API keys and tokens, plus custom regex, keyword, tenant and user-level rules. Values are replaced with placeholders, with department-based policies and role-based access for teams. File masking (PDF, DOCX) and an on-prem rule server are listed as coming soon.
differentiator: Lightweight, self-serve prompt masking aimed at small teams, with a free plan and paid tiers from $12 a month. Request-level masking and restore is fully implemented for ChatGPT only; other platforms are listed as integrations without the same restore guarantee. Early stage, launched in 2026 with a handful of extension users.

name: Lumos
capabilities: Autonomous identity governance (IGA) platform that governs access for human, non-human and AI agent identities from one live map of identities and fine-grained app permissions. Its Identity Agent Force (June 2026, successor to the 2025 Albus agent) includes an Agent Ownership Finder that catalogs AI agents and NHIs and assigns each a human owner, plus agents for access reviews, JIT access requests, role mining and dormant-NHI cleanup. MCP Governance adds inventory and policy over MCP servers and tool calls in Claude Code and Codex.
sensors: API integrations into IdPs, SaaS and cloud apps for the identity and entitlement graph. For coding agents, a lightweight hook installed in Claude Code (CLI and desktop) and Codex sends each tool call to Lumos before it runs; no gateway or traffic proxying. Custom and locally added MCP servers are discovered on first use.
protections: Requires an accountable human owner for every agent before it gets access, drafts least-privilege roles from observed usage, grants time-boxed access to people and agents and revokes it automatically, and shuts down dormant or over-scoped NHIs. The coding-agent hook returns allow/deny on MCP tool calls, Bash commands and file edits under one policy set, with a single audit trail. It does not inspect prompts or model output.
differentiator: Agent identity comes from an established IGA vendor rather than an AI-native startup: agents are governed with the same reviews, roles and JIT workflows as employees, so no new console. The MCP control is hook-based at the agent rather than a network gateway. Originally a SaaS management and access-request product (Gartner SMP Visionary, 2024) that moved into IGA and then AI agent governance. Started at Stanford; Series B ($35M, 2024) led by Scale Venture Partners with a16z.

name: WoolyAI
capabilities: Model capability monitoring for self-hosted open-weight LLMs. Detects in real time when a model starts generating restricted behavior (code, cyber/offensive activity, cryptography, tool calls) and enforces per-agent capability policy before the output reaches the agent and its tools.
sensors: Runs inside the customer's own inference runtime (e.g. vLLM serving Qwen behind an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, self-hosted or in a private VPC) and reads telemetry from the model's internals during generation, not just the prompt and response. Closed APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini) are not supported because the runtime is not under customer control.
protections: Per-agent policy on which capabilities a model may use, with Allow, Alert, Sandbox or Stop actions applied mid-generation, before generation completes and before the agent can act on the output.
differentiator: Positions itself as 'model governance' rather than guardrails or agent governance: it decides whether the model may produce a behavior at all, using in-model signals instead of an external judge model or I/O filters. The tradeoff is that it only covers open-weight models the customer hosts. The founders previously built Qumranet/KVM, Ravello Systems (acquired by Oracle) and Veertu, and WoolyAI started as a hardware-agnostic GPU hypervisor (WoolyStack, CUDA abstraction for PyTorch across NVIDIA/AMD) before pivoting to AI model security in 2026.

name: Cygrid
capabilities: Identity risk platform covering human, non-human and AI agent identities. It inventories identities across SaaS, cloud and on-prem, scores identity risk and attack paths, finds SaaS misconfigurations, shadow apps, excessive permissions and exposed tokens, and governs what enterprise access AI agents hold.
sensors: Connects by integration to the existing identity and security stack (IdPs, SaaS and cloud apps). The product is still in stealth behind a waitlist, so connector coverage and deployment details are not public.
protections: Continuous risk monitoring for permission drift and policy violations, with AI agents that remediate identity risk and push enforcement back into the identity and security stack. The company promotes runtime enforcement on agent actions (allow, restrict, pause, revoke or block before an action completes) through its ARISE framing, but has not documented how that works.
differentiator: Starts from identity risk scoring and posture rather than agent authentication or an MCP gateway, and puts AI agents in the same risk model as employees and service accounts. Early stage: Berlin GmbH registered in 2025, 1–10 staff on job postings, AI NATION grant and PwC Responsible AI program, no disclosed priced round. Founders come from Israeli intelligence units; CEO Dmitry Kharchenko was previously CTO and Chief Innovation Officer at bonify.

name: Salt Security
capabilities: Agentic Security Platform (launched March 2026) built on Salt's API security product. The Agentic Security Graph maps how agents, LLM connections, MCP servers, tools and downstream APIs relate. Agentic Security Posture Management (AG-SPM) continuously discovers shadow agents, MCP servers and APIs and governs them against a Policy Hub of 100+ posture policies, many adapted from API posture rules. Agentic Detection and Response (AG-DR) flags misuse and abnormal behavior across that graph; AI-DR (September 2026) adds LLM-layer detection of direct and indirect prompt injection, jailbreaks and unsafe model behavior. Salt Code is an MCP server that feeds security policies (OWASP API, MCP and LLM Top 10) into AI coding assistants such as Cursor, Claude Code, Copilot, Kiro and Gemini CLI.
sensors: Agentless discovery first: cloud connectors (Salt Connect for AWS, Azure, GCP), external attack-surface scanning (Salt Surface), code repositories, and an integration with Claude Enterprise for MCP discovery. Runtime visibility comes from live API traffic collected through existing gateways, WAFs, load balancers and Kubernetes (Salt Collect; 40+ integrations including Cloudflare, Kong, Apigee and AWS). Existing AI guardrails and gateways are pulled into the same view rather than replaced. Salt Code runs as an MCP server inside the coding assistant.
protections: Behavioral detection of API and agent abuse such as enumeration, logic attacks and sensitive-data exposure, tracing a request from the agent and prompt through MCP servers to the APIs and data it reaches. Blocking is pushed out through the customer's gateways and WAFs (Salt Protect, managed rules for AWS WAF) rather than an inline Salt proxy; AI-DR and AG-DR are described as detection, not inline prompt blocking. Posture findings drive drift detection and remediation of risky agent-to-API paths.
differentiator: Comes at agent security from the API layer: it argues the main risk is what agents do through MCP servers and APIs, not the prompt, and reuses years of API traffic baselining to judge agent actions. Prompt-level runtime protection is newer and detection-oriented compared with AI-native guardrail vendors. Founded in Israel (as Secful) by Roey Eliyahu and Michael Nicosia, now headquartered in Palo Alto with R&D in Tel Aviv; last priced round was a $140M Series D led by CapitalG at a $1.4B valuation (2022).

name: Vulnify
capabilities: Runtime authorization layer for AI agents: before a tool call executes, the agent asks Vulnify for a decision and gets ALLOW, REVIEW or BLOCK with a 0-100 risk score and reasons. Policies are YAML files versioned and tested in CI via a CLI (with dry-run), backed by a policy library, an agent-action risk framework and compliance mapping. Monitor mode records verdicts without enforcing; REVIEW decisions route to a human approval workflow in Slack. Also offers a free MCP server scanner and a beta gateway with an encrypted credential vault.
sensors: SaaS API called from Node and Python SDKs (a guard() wrapper around tool calls), a CLI, or a hosted MCP server that plugs into Claude, Cursor, Grok and any MCP client; integrations for the OpenAI Agents SDK and LangChain. The beta gateway sits in the request path and injects stored credentials only when a call is allowed. No self-hosted option is advertised.
protections: Pre-execution blocking or human hold of risky agent tool calls (fail-closed by default, fail-open optional), policy enforcement per tool and action, credential brokering so agents never hold raw secrets (gateway), and a hash-chained append-only audit log of every decision. Explicitly not a prompt filter: it judges the action, not the prompt text.
differentiator: Developer-first, self-serve take on agent action authorization with public pricing (free tier, Team $99/mo, Business $499/mo) and policy-as-code. Very early-stage, single-founder company operated by GZ Segurança e Defesa Cibernética LTDA in Cascavel, Brazil; founder Giovanni Zadinello is a pentester and security researcher. The brand appears to have started as a software composition analysis tool (a 'Vulnify SCA' GitHub App in 2025) before refocusing on AI agents in 2026. No disclosed funding.

name: CanaryVaults
capabilities: Deception-based security for AI apps and agents, split into six modules: CanaryVaults (decoy email identities seeded where stolen data surfaces), CanaryRAG (three invisible, plausible trap facts woven into each document so a leak into someone else's assistant or knowledge base can be proven), CanaryShield (a three-layer prompt-injection firewall: rules, semantic analyzer, sanitizer), CanaryHoneypot (decoy AI endpoints that answer with synthetic data and classify attacker intent as jailbreak, extraction, probing or normal), CanaryAudit (a SHA-256 hash-chained, tamper-evident log of actions) and CanaryAgent (heartbeats, pre-install skill scanning and a live action timeline for OpenClaw agents, plus decoy MCP tool servers added October 2026).
sensors: SaaS API with an API key: POST any untrusted string (user message, retrieved chunk, tool output) to the Shield inspect endpoint, or swap the base URL for its OpenAI-compatible proxy in front of chat completions. CanaryRAG returns the trap-laced document to store in the RAG corpus and a monitoring API queries external assistants for the planted facts. CanaryAgent is a drop-in middleware file for OpenClaw plus env vars; decoy MCP servers are added beside an agent's real tools in Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code or the OpenAI Agents SDK. No self-hosted option is advertised.
protections: Prompt-injection detection and sanitization before model execution (block or flag-only), pre-install blocking of poisoned agent skills (injection payloads, backdoors, undeclared network calls, credential harvesting), and high-signal tripwire alerts by email and Telegram when a decoy identity, honeypot endpoint, trap fact or decoy MCP tool is touched. Evidence is hash-sealed and exportable for incident and legal review.
differentiator: Applies classic canary-token deception to the AI stack: leak proof for RAG content via trap facts that survive paraphrase and re-embedding, honeypot assistants and decoy MCP tools that only a steered or malicious agent would call. Very early-stage, self-serve product with public pricing (Free, Shield $12/mo, Pro $24/mo, Enterprise $120/mo, billed via PayPal); built and run by a single India-based founder, Nagababu Pothuraju, with no formal legal entity published yet. Positions itself against Thinkst Canary and CanaryTokens. No disclosed funding.

name: Seclore
capabilities: ARMOR AI-DLP (GA May 2026) is a data-loss-prevention layer between users or apps and AI model context windows. It detects sensitive values (PII, PHI, financial records, IP) in prompts, uploaded documents and queries in real time using data type, regulatory classification and context, then replaces them with context-preserving, entropy-based tokens so the model can still reason over the data while the real values stay in the enterprise. Responses are de-tokenized for authorized users and systems.
sensors: Two modes. Portal: an enterprise gateway to ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and other browser-accessible LLMs, with policy enforcement, user management, admin controls, white labeling and usage logging, no custom development. API: a headless REST API for masking and authorized de-tokenization, plus admin and audit-log APIs, for custom LLM apps, RAG pipelines and agent frameworks. Runs as SaaS, BYOC, in-country hosted (e.g. India) or on-prem.
protections: Reversible masking or a hard block depending on context; privacy controls at the RAG retrieval layer before content enters a prompt; limits on what data AI agents can retrieve and process; per-interaction audit trail (user, prompts and files, data categories, model, policy, enforcement action) with export and AI risk dashboards. Can reuse existing Seclore classification and DRM policies.
differentiator: Established enterprise digital rights management vendor (incubated at IIT Bombay, roots in Mumbai, now headquartered in Santa Clara) whose only AI-specific product is AI-DLP; the rest of the ARMOR platform (DSPM, classification, EDRM) is classic data security rebranded for AI. Tokenize-and-restore approach rather than redact-or-block, aimed at regulated buyers in India and the Middle East (DPDP, Saudi PDPL/SAMA, NCA ECC). CEO is now Dr. Vishal Gauri. Last disclosed round: $27M Series C in 2022; total funding is an estimate. Mature company rather than an early-stage startup.

name: Kontext
capabilities: Runtime security and authorization platform for AI agents (coding assistants such as Claude Code, Codex and Claude Cowork, workplace agents and custom agents). Discovers agents in connected environments and maps the tools, systems and data each can reach; evaluates every tool call against identity-aware policy (user, session, tool, resource, parameters, credential scope) before execution and allows, escalates or denies it; flags risky behavior separately from policy decisions; tracks agent spend; and keeps a structured decision record for every action. Merlin, an open-source local classifier, judges tool calls using the user request, tool history and tool schemas.
sensors: Endpoint daemon receives tool calls from agent pre-tool hooks and decides locally; installed via Homebrew and `kontext setup` with a personal API key, or pushed to fleets as a signed MDM package. A cloud workspace holds policies and dashboards (Home, Explore, Risk, Cost, Policies) plus a Management API. Wraps MCP tool use with a runtime policy layer; covers endpoint and cloud agents. Local traces are redacted; a managed layer for shared traces is optional.
protections: Pre-execution blocking of prohibited agent actions at supported control points; least-privilege enforcement at runtime so a valid credential can still be denied when used for the wrong purpose; observe mode to preview what a policy would block before enforcing; risk detection on agent behavior; audit trail of user, tool, resource, policy decision, risk signal and outcome for investigations.
differentiator: Sits next to existing IAM/OAuth/SSO rather than replacing it, making the per-action decision those systems don't ("an agent can be properly authenticated, use an approved tool, and still take an action no one authorized"). Local-first enforcement inside the agent's own hook, with open-source components (kontext CLI in Go, Merlin classifier, sandy sandbox) and self-serve pricing from a free tier. Munich-based (legal entity Cobrowser Technology GmbH); founders come from secure computing, applied cryptography and AI systems. Emerged in Sep 2026 with a $4M round led by 42CAP; early-stage, no named customers.

name: Corgea
capabilities: AI-native AppSec platform (AI SAST, SCA, IaC, container, secrets, SBOM, AI pentest, security design review) repositioned as "security for builders & agents": an MCP server that feeds secure-coding context to coding agents (Claude Code, Copilot, Codex), scanning and auto-fixing of agent-written diffs in the IDE and at PR, and a Skills Scanning & Registry that reviews agent SKILL.md files before they can be installed.
sensors: Source-code and PR scanning with LLM-based, business-logic-aware detection; IDE integration that scans an agent's latest diff; MCP server inside the coding-agent loop; per-version static review of agent skills (instructions, declared tools, commands, package usage, requested behavior).
protections: Flags and rewrites exploitable code produced by coding agents before merge, with fixes the agent can apply itself; skills registry blocks unapproved skill versions and flags skills that exfiltrate secrets, delete files or rewrite git history, disable security tools, install untrusted packages, bypass approvals, hide instructions to ignore safety rules, or request overly broad tool access.
differentiator: Started in 2023 (YC S23, San Francisco) as an AI auto-fix layer for SAST findings and grew into a full AI-native SAST/AppSec suite; the AI-security angle is securing what coding agents write and the skills they load, not runtime protection of AI apps. Founder/CEO Ahmad Sadeddin is a 3x founder whose previous startup was acquired by Coupa. Funding: $2.6M seed (Nov 2024) led by Shorooq Partners plus YC; total is an estimate.

name: Hardalion
capabilities: "Authority infrastructure for autonomous systems": decides whether an AI agent is authorized to take a consequential action (moving money, changing enterprise records, deploying software, changing infrastructure) before it executes. Nexus is a control plane for building and running agents under explicit delegated authority; Gateway brings agents built elsewhere under the same decisions; ADAP (Agent Delegated Authority Protocol) is an open Apache 2.0 public draft (v0.1) for expressing bounded delegated authority between agents.
sensors: Sits in the agent's execution path: each intended action is evaluated against a signed authority grant (scope, purpose, amount, currency, expiry) and a signed intent by a deterministic policy engine, with no LLM in the decision. Gateway is exposed through a restricted private API; no published MCP or framework integrations.
protections: Per-action ALLOW / REQUIRE_HUMAN / BLOCK decisions, where only ALLOW reaches execution and human-required actions wait for a person; attenuation so sub-agents cannot exceed or inherit unused parent authority; intent binding so injected instructions cannot raise limits; Ed25519-signed, offline-verifiable authorization receipts for every consequential action, refused ones included; watch-then-enforce rollout mode.
differentiator: Frames the problem as authority rather than identity or access: an authenticated agent with valid credentials can still be stopped when an action exceeds what its principal delegated. Pushes this as an open protocol alongside OAuth rather than a proprietary policy language. Very early: founded 2025, Delaware-registered with a 2-10 person team, solo founder Apostolos Chardalias (software, cybersecurity, infrastructure and financial-systems background); ADAP repo published Jul 2026 with no outside adoption yet; no disclosed funding or customers.

name: Cydenti
capabilities: Non-human identity security for SaaS (NHI inventory, ISPM, ITDR, blast-radius analysis, OAuth risk) extended to AI agents: treats each AI agent and each MCP server credential (API key, OAuth token, service account) as an identity, discovers them, assigns a named human owner, maps what each can read and write, and flags segregation-of-duties conflicts (e.g. a support copilot holding both a CRM and a code-repo MCP server). AI Risk Engine adds behavioral baselining across human, machine and agent identities plus AI governance (inventory of AI tools, LLM data-leak control) and evidence for the EU AI Act, NIS2, DORA and ANSSI ReCyF.
sensors: Read-only API connectors to SaaS apps, OAuth apps and identity providers (18+ native integrations; Microsoft 365/Entra ID, Google Workspace, Salesforce among them); no agent to install, no code changes. Discovers MCP servers and agents through the same connectors. Hosted in the EU (Hetzner Germany, OVHcloud, Scaleway).
protections: Detection only: ownerless and dormant credentials, permission drift, unrotated keys, toxic permission combinations, hijacked service accounts and abused tokens (MITRE ATT&CK-aligned), anomalous agent behavior such as an agent suddenly bulk-pulling CRM records. Explicitly not an MCP gateway and does not sit in the agent session; revocation and rotation are pushed back to the customer's existing IAM/PAM.
differentiator: European-sovereign, read-only NHI platform aimed at SMB and mid-market under EU regulation, positioned as an alternative to US NHI vendors (Astrix, Entro). AI-security angle is identity visibility and ownership for agents and MCP credentials, not prompt or runtime protection. Selected CYBIAH provider (Campus Cyber with Hub France IA). Founded in Paris in 2024 by Addy Sharma (15+ years of banking cybersecurity at AXA and BPCE) and Christophe Graignic; bootstrapped through consulting, then an undisclosed pre-seed; very early, ~10 client companies.
